entries.name: Redguard
entries.summary: The people of Hammerfell, descended from the Yokudans who crossed the sea. Born athletes and the finest swordsmen in Tamriel.

entries.name: Orsimer
entries.summary: The Orcs, children of Malacath, living in strongholds across the north. Superb smiths and heavy-armoured fighters, long scorned by the other races.

entries.name: Nord
entries.summary: The tall, fair people of Skyrim, hardened by its cold. Fierce warriors and seafarers who prize courage, mead and the Voice of their ancestors.

entries.name: Khajiit
entries.summary: The cat-folk of Elsweyr. Their shape depends on the phases of the moons at birth, from the near-human Ohmes to the great Senche. Quick, agile and fond of moon sugar.

entries.name: Imperial
entries.summary: The people of Cyrodiil, heart of the Empire. Diplomats, traders and soldiers of the Legion, known for their discipline and silver tongues.

entries.name: Dunmer
entries.summary: The Dark Elves of Morrowind: grey-skinned, red-eyed, fire-blooded. Ruled by Great Houses and the Tribunal Temple, wary of outsiders.

entries.name: Breton
entries.summary: The people of High Rock, mixed Nedic and Elven blood. Born with a feel for magic and a natural resistance to it; their kingdoms quarrel endlessly.

entries.name: Bosmer
entries.summary: The Wood Elves of Valenwood: quick, nimble and the best archers in Tamriel. Their Green Pact forbids harming the forest, so they eat only meat.

entries.name: Argonian
entries.summary: The scaled people of Black Marsh, bound to the Hist trees of their homeland. Breathe water, shrug off disease, and are rarely trusted by the Dunmer next door.

entries.name: Altmer
entries.summary: The High Elves of the Summerset Isles: tall, golden-skinned and proud of the oldest Aldmeri blood. Gifted mages, often thought aloof by the other races.

entries.name: The Warrior
entries.summary: Guardian sign of Last Seed, protector of the Lady, Steed and Lord. Its children are held to be quick-tempered and handy with weapons.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Mage
entries.summary: Guardian sign of Rain's Hand, protector of the Apprentice, Atronach and Ritual. Its children are gifted casters, but said to be proud and forgetful.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Thief
entries.summary: Guardian sign of Evening Star, protector of the Lover, Shadow and Tower. Its children court danger and dodge it, until their luck runs dry.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Lady
entries.summary: Charge of the Warrior, rising in Hearthfire. Those born under her are thought to be gentle and forgiving.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Steed
entries.summary: Charge of the Warrior, rising in Midyear. Its children are said to be restless and always in a hurry to be elsewhere.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Lord
entries.summary: Charge of the Warrior, rising in First Seed. Its children are thought hardy and healthy; some call them Trollkin for a weakness to fire.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Apprentice
entries.summary: Charge of the Mage, rising in Sun's Height. Its children take to magic easily, yet magic also bites them harder.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Atronach
entries.summary: Charge of the Mage, rising in Sun's Dusk. Its children hold deep wells of magicka but cannot refill them on their own.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Ritual
entries.summary: Charge of the Mage, rising in Morning Star. Its gifts are said to shift with the moons and planets; often linked with healing and mending.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Lover
entries.summary: Charge of the Thief, rising in Sun's Dawn. Those born under it are thought graceful and full of passion.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Shadow
entries.summary: Charge of the Thief, rising in Second Seed. Its children are said to slip into darkness and go unseen.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Tower
entries.summary: Charge of the Thief, rising in Frostfall. Its children are said to sniff out gold and get past any lock.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: The Serpent
entries.summary: The thirteenth sign: belongs to no season and no guardian, drifting across the sky. Its children are both the most blessed and the most cursed.
entries.eraNote: Timeless astrology; the same 13 signs are used in 3E 433.

entries.name: Morning Star
entries.summary: Month 1 of 12, 31 days, a winter month. Ruled by The Ritual. Argonian (Jel) name: Vakka, "Sun".

entries.name: Sun's Dawn
entries.summary: Month 2 of 12, 28 days, a spring month. Ruled by The Lover. Argonian (Jel) name: Xeech, "Nut". Some texts give it a 29th day.

entries.name: First Seed
entries.summary: Month 3 of 12, 31 days, a spring month. Ruled by The Lord. Argonian (Jel) name: Sisei, "Sprout".

entries.name: Rain's Hand
entries.summary: Month 4 of 12, 30 days, a spring month. Ruled by The Mage. Argonian (Jel) name: Hist-Deek, "Hist sapling".

entries.name: Second Seed
entries.summary: Month 5 of 12, 31 days, a summer month. Ruled by The Shadow. Argonian (Jel) name: Hist-Dooka, "mature Hist".

entries.name: Midyear
entries.summary: Month 6 of 12, 30 days, a summer month. Ruled by The Steed. Argonian (Jel) name: Hist-Tsoko, "elder Hist".

entries.name: Sun's Height
entries.summary: Month 7 of 12, 31 days, a summer month. Ruled by The Apprentice. Argonian (Jel) name: Thtithil-Gah, "egg-basket".

entries.name: Last Seed
entries.summary: Month 8 of 12, 31 days, a autumn month. Ruled by The Warrior. Argonian (Jel) name: Thtithil, "egg".

entries.name: Hearthfire
entries.summary: Month 9 of 12, 30 days, a autumn month. Ruled by The Lady. Argonian (Jel) name: Nushmeeko, "lizard". Oblivion spells it Heartfire.

entries.name: Frostfall
entries.summary: Month 10 of 12, 31 days, a autumn month. Ruled by The Tower. Argonian (Jel) name: Shaja-Nushmeeko, "semi-humanoid lizard".

entries.name: Sun's Dusk
entries.summary: Month 11 of 12, 30 days, a winter month. Ruled by The Atronach. Argonian (Jel) name: Saxhleel, "Argonian".

entries.name: Evening Star
entries.summary: Month 12 of 12, 31 days, a winter month. Ruled by The Thief. Argonian (Jel) name: Xulomaht, "the deceased".

entries.summary: Day 1 of the 7-day Tamrielic week. Oblivion opens on Morndas, 27th of Last Seed, 3E 433.

entries.summary: Day 6 of the 7-day Tamrielic week.

entries.name: Acrobat
entries.summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Endurance. A nimble type who trusts agility and stamina and does not fear a long leap.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Agent
entries.summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Personality. Smooth talker in company, hard to spot once out of the light.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Archer
entries.summary: Combat specialization; favoured Agility, Strength. Fights from range and aims to drop a foe before blades are drawn.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Assassin
entries.summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Intelligence, Speed. Quiet and quick, strikes the unaware from the dark; locks rarely stop them.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Barbarian
entries.summary: Combat specialization; favoured Speed, Strength. Fast, brutal fighter who skips heavy plate and simply overpowers the enemy.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Bard
entries.summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Intelligence, Personality. Sharp and sociable; tries words first and the sword second.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Battlemage
entries.summary: Magic specialization; favoured Intelligence, Strength. Half scholar, half soldier, equally ready with a spell or a weapon.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Crusader
entries.summary: Combat specialization; favoured Strength, Willpower. Heavy hitter who patches their own wounds with restoration between fights.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Healer
entries.summary: Magic specialization; favoured Personality, Willpower. Battles sickness and poison with restoration, and uses destruction when pressed.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Knight
entries.summary: Combat specialization; favoured Personality, Strength. The noble fighter: strong of arm and of character.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Mage
entries.summary: Magic specialization; favoured Intelligence, Willpower. Relies on broad magical learning, which they hold to be stronger than steel.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Monk
entries.summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Willpower. Strong-willed and quick, fights with bare hands or the bow.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Nightblade
entries.summary: Magic specialization; favoured Speed, Willpower. Moves fast through shadow and uses spells to tilt the odds.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Pilgrim
entries.summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Endurance, Personality. Tough, well-read traveller who gets by through trade and persuasion.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Rogue
entries.summary: Combat specialization; favoured Personality, Speed. Quick rather than strong, with a tongue as sharp as the blade.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Scout
entries.summary: Combat specialization; favoured Endurance, Speed. Prefers the open country to town life; good at avoiding harm and guarding themselves.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Sorcerer
entries.summary: Magic specialization; favoured Endurance, Intelligence. A caster tough enough to wear heavy armour while slinging spells.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Spellsword
entries.summary: Magic specialization; favoured Endurance, Willpower. Blend of fighter and caster, more agile than a sorcerer and less predictable.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Thief
entries.summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Speed. Lives off other people's losses: quick in the shadows, shrewd at the market.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Warrior
entries.summary: Combat specialization; favoured Endurance, Strength. Melee generalist who charges in and has little use for magic.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Witchhunter
entries.summary: Magic specialization; favoured Agility, Intelligence. Light on their feet and clever with spells, keeps foes at a distance with arrows.
entries.eraNote: Standard class in both 2006 Oblivion and Remastered.

entries.name: Custom class (default name "Adventurer")
entries.summary: Player-built class: pick a specialization, two favoured attributes and seven major skills. Oblivion names it Adventurer by default; any name allowed.

entries.name: Cyrodiil
entries.summary: Imperial heartland and seat of the Empire. In 3E 433 the Emperor is murdered and the Ruby Throne left empty; ruled meanwhile by Chancellor Ocato and the Elder Council.

entries.name: Black Marsh
entries.summary: Argonian swamp province in the southeast. An Imperial province in 3E 433, recently at war with its Dunmer neighbours (Arnesian War).
entries.eraNote: Imperial province in 3E 433; seceded between 4E 1 and 4E 29.

entries.name: Elsweyr
entries.summary: Khajiit province of deserts and jungles. In the late 3E a confederacy within the Empire, prospering on moon sugar trade and feuding with Leyawiin at the border.
entries.eraNote: Imperial province in 3E 433; seceded between 4E 1 and 4E 29.

entries.name: Hammerfell
entries.summary: Redguard desert province in the west. Part of the Empire in 3E 433; it later walks away from the Empire after the Great War of 4E 171 to 175.
entries.eraNote: Imperial province in 3E 433; renounced by the Empire in 4E 175.

entries.name: High Rock
entries.summary: Breton province of rival kingdoms around the Iliac Bay. Loyal to the Empire in 3E 433; its map was redrawn by the Warp in the West of 3E 417.
entries.eraNote: Imperial province in 3E 433 and still in 4E 201.

entries.name: Morrowind
entries.summary: Dunmer homeland. In 3E 433 an Imperial province with wide autonomy under the Armistice; its gods are gone or missing after 3E 427, but the Red Year has not happened yet.
entries.eraNote: Imperial province in 3E 433; Red Year 4E 5; left the Empire before 4E 48.

entries.name: Skyrim
entries.summary: Cold northern Nord province. Part of the Empire in 3E 433, the year its Nords take all of Solstheim.

entries.name: Summerset Isles
entries.summary: Altmer island province in the southwest. In 3E 433 still ruled by its old monarchy inside the Empire; renamed Alinor only after the Thalmor coup of 4E 22.
entries.eraNote: Imperial province in 3E 433. "Alinor" as a province name is 4E (future).

entries.name: Valenwood
entries.summary: Bosmer forest province in the southwest. Part of the Empire in 3E 433 with an Empire-friendly government until the Thalmor-backed coup of 4E 29.
entries.eraNote: Imperial province in 3E 433; Dominion member only from 4E 29.

entries.name: Orsinium (Orc kingdom, not a province)
entries.summary: Orc city-state between Wayrest and the Wrothgarian Mountains, refounded by Gortwog in 3E 399. Its bid to become a full province was still under review in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Not a province in 3E 433: application pending. Sacked again in early 4E.

entries.name: Heartlands
entries.summary: Central grassy lowland around Lake Rumare and the Upper Niben, with the Imperial City at its heart.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Great Forest
entries.summary: Huge crescent of woodland wrapping round the Heartlands on three sides; Chorrol lies on its edge.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Colovian Highlands
entries.summary: Hilly, wooded far west of Cyrodiil, remote from Imperial centres and known for strong red wine.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Gold Coast
entries.summary: Cyrodiil's western coastline between the Brena and the Strid; home of the port of Anvil and of Kvatch.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: West Weald
entries.summary: Open Colovian countryside in the southwest, famous for vineyards and tomatoes; Skingrad is its city.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Jerall Mountains
entries.summary: Snowy northern range on the Skyrim border; Bruma and Cloud Ruler Temple sit here.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Nibenay Basin
entries.summary: Eastern farmland of the Niben valley, heartland of the Nibenese; Cheydinhal lies near its eastern hills.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Nibenay Valley
entries.summary: Humid, river-cut south of the Niben running down to Niben Bay; Bravil is its city.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Blackwood
entries.summary: Swampy far south around Leyawiin, bordering Black Marsh and draining into Topal Bay.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Valus Mountains
entries.summary: Eastern range on the Morrowind border, meeting the Jeralls and Velothi range at Mount Trolhetta.
entries.eraNote: One of the 10 regions of Cyrodiil in Oblivion.

entries.name: Imperial City
entries.summary: Capital of Cyrodiil and the Empire on City Isle in Lake Rumare; its Temple of the One honours Akatosh.

entries.name: Anvil
entries.summary: Port city of the far southwest; patron Dibella; notable Redguard and Bosmer residents.

entries.name: Bravil
entries.summary: Damp river town on Niben Bay, called the poorest in Cyrodiil; patron Mara.

entries.name: Bruma
entries.summary: Snowbound northern city with many Nords; patron Talos.

entries.name: Cheydinhal
entries.summary: Northeastern city with many Dunmer and Orcs; patron Arkay.

entries.name: Chorrol
entries.summary: Northwestern city at the edge of the Great Forest; patron Stendarr.

entries.name: Kvatch
entries.summary: Hill city of Akatosh, overrun and burned by Daedra from the first Oblivion Gate in 3E 433. A "Kvatch refugee" is a strong era origin.
entries.eraNote: Exists in 3E 433 but destroyed at the start of the Crisis (Last Seed 3E 433).

entries.name: Leyawiin
entries.summary: Southern city near Black Marsh and Elsweyr with many Argonians and Khajiit; patron Zenithar.

entries.name: Skingrad
entries.summary: Wine city of the southwest, split into two districts by bridges; patron Julianos.

entries.name: Arboretum
entries.summary: Imperial City district. Park district of statues and trees.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Elven Gardens District
entries.summary: Imperial City district. Residential quarter in the northwest of the city.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Market District
entries.summary: Imperial City district. Commercial quarter with most shops and services.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Talos Plaza District
entries.summary: Imperial City district. Well-off residential quarter with a dragon statue at its centre.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Temple District
entries.summary: Imperial City district. Residential quarter around the Temple of the One.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Waterfront District
entries.summary: Imperial City district. The docks on City Isle's southwest shore; poor, and home turf of the Thieves Guild.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Arena District
entries.summary: Imperial City district. Eastern quarter built around the Arena.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Green Emperor Way
entries.summary: Imperial City district. Cemetery and gardens at the core, around the Imperial Palace.
entries.eraNote: District of the Imperial City in 3E 433.

entries.name: Aleswell
entries.summary: Roadside village whose folk are said to have vanished; rumoured haunted until its quest is solved.

entries.name: Blankenmarch
entries.summary: Tiny hamlet of three houses and a garden in the south.

entries.name: Bleaker's Way
entries.summary: Village founded by Ulf the Bleaker; run by the rival Ulfgar and Dalvilu families.

entries.name: Border Watch
entries.summary: Khajiit village near Elsweyr, built in Leyawiin style, bound to the K'Sharra Prophecy.

entries.name: Brindle Home
entries.summary: Small village where one resident has angered a Daedric Prince.

entries.name: Cropsford
entries.summary: Village wrecked by two feuding goblin tribes and rebuilt with outside help.

entries.name: Hackdirt
entries.summary: Mining village with a dark cult secret; very hostile to outsiders.

entries.name: Harlun's Watch
entries.summary: Quiet village troubled by strange lights from a nearby cave.

entries.name: Pell's Gate
entries.summary: Small Heartlands village, once home of the swordswoman known as Umbra.

entries.name: Water's Edge
entries.summary: Riverside hamlet near Leyawiin, massacred by the Blackwood Company during the Fighters Guild story.

entries.name: Weye
entries.summary: Tiny Heartlands hamlet: one house and the Wawnet Inn.

entries.name: The Nine Divines (Imperial Cult, "the Chapel")
entries.summary: State faith of the Empire: the Eight plus Talos. In Cyrodiil simply called the Church or Chapel; each city chapel honours one patron Divine.
entries.eraNote: Majority faith in 3E 433; Talos worship fully legal.

entries.name: Daedra worship
entries.summary: Private devotion to a Daedric Prince at a shrine. Legal but frowned on; mainstream priests sometimes lead witch hunts against worshippers.
entries.eraNote: Present in 3E 433: 15 open shrines in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Tribunal Temple (Dunmer)
entries.summary: Old faith of Morrowind in Almalexia, Sotha Sil and Vivec. By 3E 433 two are dead and Vivec is missing; the Temple is shaken but standing.
entries.eraNote: Current but in crisis after 3E 427. See race research for detail.

entries.name: New Temple (Dunmer)
entries.summary: Post-Red Year Dunmer faith that returned to the "Good Daedra" and demoted the Tribunal to saints.
entries.eraNote: Forms after the Red Year of 4E 5. Not allowed in 3E 433.

entries.name: Racial and regional pantheons (pointer)
entries.summary: Each culture has its own pantheon (Nordic, Yokudan, Khajiiti, Bosmeri, Hist, Orcish etc.). Covered per race by other research; see Lore:Religions.

entries.name: Akatosh
entries.summary: Dragon God of Time and chief of the Nine; stands for endurance and loyal service. Patron of Kvatch; the Temple of the One in the Imperial City is his.

entries.name: Arkay
entries.summary: God of the cycle of birth and death and of the turning seasons; keeper of burial rites. Patron of Cheydinhal.

entries.name: Dibella
entries.summary: Goddess of beauty, art and love, one of the most popular Divines. Patron of Anvil.

entries.name: Julianos
entries.summary: God of wisdom, logic, law and magic; his temples teach letters and law. Patron of Skingrad.

entries.name: Kynareth
entries.summary: Goddess of sky, wind and rain, protector of sailors and travellers. The only Divine with no city chapel in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Mara
entries.summary: Mother goddess of love and compassion; she blesses marriages. Patron of Bravil.

entries.name: Stendarr
entries.summary: God of mercy, justice and righteous strength in defence of the weak. Patron of Chorrol.

entries.name: Zenithar
entries.summary: God of work, trade and honestly earned wealth. Patron of Leyawiin.

entries.name: Talos
entries.summary: Tiber Septim raised to godhood: patron of the Empire, its ideals and its soldiers. Patron of Bruma.
entries.eraNote: Worship legal in 3E 433. The Talos ban comes with the White-Gold Concordat after 4E 175 (future).

entries.name: Azura
entries.summary: Prince of dusk and dawn, twilight and prophecy; long revered by the Dunmer. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Boethiah
entries.summary: Prince of plots, deceit and betrayal (spelled Boethia in Oblivion). Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Clavicus Vile
entries.summary: Prince of wishes, deals and bargains, usually with a catch. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Hermaeus Mora
entries.summary: Prince of forbidden knowledge, memory and fate. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Hircine
entries.summary: Prince of the hunt and of beasts; father of lycanthropy. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Malacath
entries.summary: Prince of outcasts, oaths and curses; god of the Orcs. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Mehrunes Dagon
entries.summary: Prince of destruction, upheaval and ambition; his invasion is the Oblivion Crisis. No open shrine; a hidden one lies in Lake Arrius Caverns.
entries.eraNote: Worship in 3E 433 means the Mythic Dawn: hostile to the Empire.

entries.name: Mephala
entries.summary: Prince of lies, secrets and webs of intrigue. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Meridia
entries.summary: Prince of life and light; sworn enemy of the undead. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Molag Bal
entries.summary: Prince of domination and enslavement; source of vampirism. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Namira
entries.summary: Prince of decay and of things others find revolting; patron of outcasts and beggars. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Nocturnal
entries.summary: Prince of night, shadow and luck; patron of thieves. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Peryite
entries.summary: Prince of plague and pestilence, who keeps order in the lowest realms. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Sanguine
entries.summary: Prince of revelry, excess and indulgence. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Sheogorath
entries.summary: Prince of madness, lord of the Shivering Isles. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Vaermina
entries.summary: Prince of dreams, nightmares and omens. Has a shrine in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Jyggalag
entries.summary: Prince of order, long cursed to live as Sheogorath and freed only during each Greymarch. Has no shrine in Cyrodiil.
entries.eraNote: Freed in the Greymarch of 3E 433 (Shivering Isles). Rare, but lore-valid.

entries.name: Ithelia
entries.summary: Forgotten Prince of paths and possibilities; remembered by almost no one.
entries.eraNote: Erased from mortal memory; per UESP only Hermaeus Mora and the Vestige (2E 582) recall her. Not worshippable in 3E 433.

entries.name: Fighters Guild
entries.summary: Chartered guild of hired swords with halls in every city. In 3E 433 led by Vilena Donton and under pressure from the Blackwood Company.

entries.name: Mages Guild
entries.summary: Guild of scholars and casters, centred on the Arcane University. Arch-Mage Hannibal Traven (chosen 3E 431) has banned necromancy.

entries.summary: Rank 1 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.name: Apprentice
entries.summary: Rank 2 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.summary: Rank 3 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.summary: Rank 4 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.summary: Rank 5 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.summary: Rank 8 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.name: Master-Wizard
entries.summary: Rank 9 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.name: Arch-Mage
entries.summary: Rank 10 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

entries.name: Thieves Guild
entries.summary: Outlawed but tolerated guild led by the Gray Fox. House rules: never steal from members, never kill on a job, never rob the poor.

entries.name: Pickpocket
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Footpad
entries.summary: Rank 2 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Bandit
entries.summary: Rank 3 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Prowler
entries.summary: Rank 4 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Cat Burglar
entries.summary: Rank 5 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Shadowfoot
entries.summary: Rank 6 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Master Thief
entries.summary: Rank 7 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Gray Fox
entries.summary: Rank 8 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

entries.name: Dark Brotherhood
entries.summary: Secret guild of assassins serving Sithis and the Night Mother, bound by the Five Tenets and run by the Black Hand.

entries.name: Murderer
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Slayer
entries.summary: Rank 2 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Eliminator
entries.summary: Rank 3 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Assassin
entries.summary: Rank 4 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Executioner
entries.summary: Rank 5 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Silencer
entries.summary: Rank 6 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Speaker
entries.summary: Rank 7 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Listener
entries.summary: Rank 8 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Arena (Imperial City)
entries.summary: Blood sport in the Imperial City; fighters join the Blue or Yellow team and climb toward Grand Champion.

entries.name: Pit Dog
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Brawler
entries.summary: Rank 2 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Bloodletter
entries.summary: Rank 3 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Myrmidon
entries.summary: Rank 4 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Warrior
entries.summary: Rank 5 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Gladiator
entries.summary: Rank 6 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Hero
entries.summary: Rank 7 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Champion
entries.summary: Rank 8 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Grand Champion
entries.summary: Rank 9 of 9 in the Arena.

entries.name: Knights of the Nine
entries.summary: Holy order hunting the relics of the Divine Crusader. Founded 3E 111 by Sir Amiel Lannus, disbanded 3E 131, revived in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Current: revived in 3E 433 (Knights of the Nine content).

entries.name: Pilgrim
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 4 in the Knights of the Nine (Divine Crusader is unique).

entries.name: Knight Errant
entries.summary: Rank 2 of 4 in the Knights of the Nine (Divine Crusader is unique).

entries.name: Knight Commander
entries.summary: Rank 3 of 4 in the Knights of the Nine (Divine Crusader is unique).

entries.name: Divine Crusader
entries.summary: Rank 4 of 4 in the Knights of the Nine (Divine Crusader is unique).

entries.name: Nine Divines (chapel faction)
entries.summary: The priests and staff of the city chapels. Outsiders can enter only as a Pilgrim.

entries.name: Pilgrim
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 1 in the chapel faction (only rank open to outsiders).

entries.name: Order of the Dragon
entries.summary: Imperial knightly order founded by Tiber Septim. Its highest honour, Champion of Cyrodiil, has had only seven holders.
entries.eraNote: Current in 3E 433. Champion title is unique (the Hero of Kvatch).

entries.name: Champion of Cyrodiil
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 1 in the Order of the Dragon (unique, not for player cards).

entries.name: Knights of the Thorn
entries.summary: Small knightly order sworn to protect Cheydinhal, led by the count's son Farwil Indarys; lodge outside the west gate.

entries.name: Honorary Knight
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 1 in the Knights of the Thorn (honorary).

entries.name: Knights of the White Stallion
entries.summary: Chivalric order chartered by Count Marius Caro of Leyawiin to stamp out banditry in the Lower Niben.

entries.name: Knight-Errant
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 1 in the Knights of the White Stallion.

entries.name: Blades
entries.summary: The Emperor's secret bodyguard and spies, based at Cloud Ruler Temple and led by Grandmaster Jauffre in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Current in 3E 433. Outlawed only after the Great War (4E 175).

entries.name: Knight Brother / Knight Sister
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 3 in the Blades (only the first is open in-game).

entries.name: Captain
entries.summary: Rank 2 of 3 in the Blades (only the first is open in-game).

entries.name: Grandmaster
entries.summary: Rank 3 of 3 in the Blades (only the first is open in-game).

entries.name: Imperial Legion
entries.summary: The Empire's army: garrisons forts, patrols roads and keeps the peace. Not joinable in Oblivion, but fine for RP backstory.

entries.name: Imperial Watch (Imperial City guard)
entries.summary: Legion soldiers who police the Imperial City, led by watch captains such as Hieronymus Lex.

entries.name: County guard
entries.summary: Each county's own soldiers, serving its count or countess rather than the Legion; uniforms show the city's sigil.

entries.name: Nobility of Cyrodiil
entries.summary: Landed families of the counties. Their power is limited: real authority sits with the Chancellor and Elder Council.

entries.name: Elder Council
entries.summary: Governing council of the Empire; with the throne empty in 3E 433 it rules under High Chancellor Ocato.

entries.name: Order of the Virtuous Blood
entries.summary: Citizen vampire-hunting society in the Temple District of the Imperial City; pays a bounty for vampire dust.

entries.name: Blackwood Company
entries.summary: Cut-price mercenary outfit from Leyawiin, rival to the Fighters Guild, willing to take dirty work.

entries.name: Necromancers (Order of the Black Worm)
entries.summary: Mannimarco's followers, at war with the Mages Guild since necromancy was banned.

entries.name: Mythic Dawn
entries.summary: Doomsday cult of Mehrunes Dagon that murdered Uriel VII and his heirs and opens the Oblivion Gates. Hostile: secret villain RP only.
entries.eraNote: Current and hostile in 3E 433; a revived cult also appears 4E 200.

entries.name: Initiate
entries.summary: Rank 1 of 2 in the Mythic Dawn as seen by the player.

entries.name: Acolyte
entries.summary: Rank 2 of 2 in the Mythic Dawn as seen by the player.

entries.name: Thalmor
entries.summary: Altmer supremacist movement that resurfaced shortly before 3E 433 and was mostly ignored at the time.
entries.eraNote: Fringe in 3E 433, no power until the 4E 22 coup. Allow only as a hidden fringe sympathy, never as an agent.

entries.name: First Aldmeri Dominion
entries.summary: Queen Ayrenn's alliance founded 2E 580; one of the three ESO-era alliances.
entries.eraNote: 2E 580 to 2E 582 era. Ancestry or heritage only.

entries.name: Second Aldmeri Dominion
entries.summary: Elven union said to have formed around 2E 830 when Summerset took Valenwood.

entries.name: Third Aldmeri Dominion
entries.summary: Thalmor-run elven empire of Alinor and Valenwood that later fights the Great War.
entries.eraNote: Formed 4E 29 after the 4E 22 coup. Not allowed.

entries.name: Ebonheart Pact
entries.summary: ESO-era alliance of Nords, Dunmer and Argonians born of the Akaviri invasion of 2E 572.

entries.name: Daggerfall Covenant
entries.summary: ESO-era alliance of Bretons, Redguards and Orcs that marched on Cyrodiil in 2E 582.
entries.eraNote: First Covenant 2E 542; ESO era 2E 582. Heritage only.

entries.name: Stormcloaks
entries.summary: Ulfric Stormcloak's Nord rebels against the Empire and the Talos ban.
entries.eraNote: Skyrim era, swelling in 4E 201. Not allowed.

entries.name: Dawnguard
entries.summary: Vampire hunters of the Rift in Skyrim, reborn under Isran.
entries.eraNote: Old 2E roots, but the active order is reformed in 4E 201. Not allowed.

entries.name: Mede Dynasty
entries.summary: Imperial dynasty founded when Titus Mede took the Imperial City.

entries.name: Emperor of Tamriel
entries.summary: Head of the Empire. Uriel Septim VII is murdered in 3E 433; his hidden son Martin is the last Septim heir.

entries.name: High Chancellor
entries.summary: Head of the Elder Council; in 3E 433 Ocato holds the Empire together.

entries.name: Knight
entries.summary: Noble rank 1 of 5 in Oblivion's hidden Nobility faction.

entries.name: Baron / Baroness
entries.summary: Noble rank 2 of 5 in Oblivion's hidden Nobility faction.

entries.name: Lord / Lady
entries.summary: Noble rank 3 of 5 in Oblivion's hidden Nobility faction.

entries.name: Count / Countess
entries.summary: Noble rank 4 of 5 in Oblivion's hidden Nobility faction.

entries.name: Duke / Duchess
entries.summary: Noble rank 5 of 5 in Oblivion's hidden Nobility faction.

entries.name: Countess of Anvil
entries.summary: Millona Umbranox rules; her husband Count Corvus is absent. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Count of Bravil
entries.summary: Regulus Terentius rules; his son Gellius is his heir. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Countess of Bruma
entries.summary: Narina Carvain rules from Castle Bruma. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Count of Cheydinhal
entries.summary: Andel Indarys, a Dunmer, rules; son Farwil leads the Knights of the Thorn. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Countess of Chorrol
entries.summary: Arriana Valga rules after the death of her husband Charus. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Count of Kvatch
entries.summary: Ormellius Goldwine dies in the Daedric attack on Kvatch in 3E 433. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Count of Leyawiin
entries.summary: Marius Caro rules and charters the Knights of the White Stallion. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Count of Skingrad
entries.summary: Janus Hassildor rules, a reclusive count rarely seen in public. Unique NPC title, not for player cards.

entries.name: Merits (after the Ten Commands)
entries.summary: MESOL grouping: good qualities drawn from the Ten Commands of the Nine Divines and the old Imperial virtues. Not called Virtues: Remastered uses that word for level-up points.

entries.name: Flaws
entries.summary: MESOL grouping: failings, several taken from the temperaments the birthsigns are said to give.

entries.name: Charitable
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Gives to the needy and shields the weak (Stendarr's command).

entries.name: Reverent
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Honours the land, its creatures and the dead (Arkay's command).

entries.name: Devoted
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Puts home, family and peace first (Mara's command).

entries.name: Industrious
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Works hard, spends wisely, never steals (Zenithar's command).

entries.name: Valiant
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Bold against evil, ready to defend others (Talos's command).

entries.name: Nature-wise
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Uses what the wild gives with care and respects its fury (Kynareth's command).

entries.name: Romantic
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Open to art, love and friendship (Dibella's command).

entries.name: Lawful
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Seeks the truth, keeps the law, asks the wise (Julianos's command).

entries.name: Dutiful
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Serves the Emperor and does their duty (Akatosh's command).

entries.name: Pious
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Keeps faith and its rites; one of the Imperial virtues.

entries.name: Discreet
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Knows when to keep quiet; one of the Imperial virtues.

entries.name: Loyal
entries.summary: Merit (MESOL suggestion). Stands by liege, guild and friends; one of the Imperial virtues.

entries.name: Hot-tempered
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Quick to anger; the temper said of Warrior-born.

entries.name: Arrogant
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Thinks too highly of their own mind; a failing said of Mage-born.

entries.name: Absent-minded
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Forgets the everyday while lost in thought; also said of Mage-born.

entries.name: Impatient
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Always rushing to the next place; the restlessness said of Steed-born.

entries.name: Reckless
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Takes risks for the thrill and trusts luck too far, like the Thief-born.

entries.name: Greedy
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Wants more coin than honest work brings; breaks Zenithar's command.

entries.name: Cowardly
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Backs away from danger and from others in need; fails Talos's command.

entries.name: Slothful
entries.summary: Flaw (MESOL suggestion). Sloppy and idle, avoids hard work; the opposite of Industrious.

entries.name: Alfiq
entries.summary: Tiny four-legged furstock about the size of a housecat, without thumbs. Born when Masser wanes and Secunda is full.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology, not era-bound; depicted in ESO and Legends

entries.name: Alfiq-raht
entries.summary: Quadruped furstock a little bigger than the Alfiq; little else is recorded. Born when Masser wanes and Secunda waxes.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; only a Second Era reference exists

entries.name: Cathay
entries.summary: Upright, plantigrade, fully furred Khajiit of roughly Man or Mer size with a long tail. UESP captions an Oblivion Khajiit as Cathay. Born Masser waxing, Secunda full.
entries.eraNote: UESP image caption 'A Cathay (Oblivion)' and 'A Cathay (Skyrim)'

entries.name: Cathay-raht
entries.summary: A bigger, stronger Cathay, known as front-line infantry in the Five Year War with Valenwood. Born when both Masser and Secunda wax.
entries.eraNote: Five Year War (3E 395 to ca. 3E 399) gives late Third Era evidence

entries.name: Dagi
entries.summary: One of the smallest furstocks, with a lynx-like face. Born when Masser wanes and Secunda is new.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; depicted in ESO and Legends

entries.name: Dagi-raht
entries.summary: Two-legged, lynx-faced furstock, slightly larger than the Dagi but still short. Born when both moons wane.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; depicted in ESO and Legends

entries.name: Ohmes
entries.summary: Elf-like, furless biped who often paints a feline face; the Arena-era look. Born when Masser is new and Secunda full.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; UESP links Ohmes to Arena depictions

entries.name: Ohmes-raht
entries.summary: Human-built plantigrade biped with thin fur and a tail; the Daggerfall-era look. Born when Masser is new and Secunda waxes.

entries.name: Pahmar
entries.summary: Giant, tiger-like biped, smaller only than the Pahmar-raht. Born when Masser is full and Secunda new.

entries.name: Pahmar-raht
entries.summary: Very tall plantigrade giant that looks much like a senche-tiger on two legs. Born when Masser is full and Secunda wanes.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; depicted in ESO and Legends

entries.name: Senche
entries.summary: Large four-legged furstock with tawny fur and blood-red stripes and an apelike build. Born when both moons are full.

entries.name: Senche-raht
entries.summary: The largest furstock, a quadruped nicknamed the battlecat, said to be the longest-lived. Born when Masser is full and Secunda waxes.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; depicted in ESO and Legends

entries.name: Suthay
entries.summary: Digitigrade biped, shorter than the Suthay-raht. Born when both moons are new.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; ESO statue and Legends

entries.name: Suthay-raht
entries.summary: Man-height digitigrade biped with full fur, tail and cat head; the Morrowind and Redguard look. Born when Masser is new and Secunda wanes.
entries.eraNote: Common on Vvardenfell toward the end of the Third Era

entries.name: Tojay
entries.summary: Little-known furstock said to resemble the Cathay; sources disagree on its leg type. Born when Masser waxes and Secunda is new.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; only an ESO statue depicts it

entries.name: Tojay-raht
entries.summary: Digitigrade biped, larger than the Tojay. Born when Masser waxes and Secunda wanes.
entries.eraNote: Birth-determined morphology; only an ESO statue depicts it

entries.name: Mane
entries.summary: Unique Khajiit born only when Masser and Secunda align. Tradition holds a single Mane lives at a time and is reborn. Not a player option.
entries.eraNote: An unnamed Mane negotiated the Leyawiin border ca. 3E 432

entries.name: Masser (Jode)
entries.summary: The larger moon. Khajiit call it Jode, the red lantern of love. Its phase at birth is one half of a Khajiit's furstock.

entries.name: Secunda (Jone)
entries.summary: The smaller moon. Khajiit call it Jone, the pale lantern of mercy. Its phase at birth is the other half of a Khajiit's furstock.

entries.name: Full
entries.summary: One of four phases used in the furstock birth table, applied separately to Masser and Secunda.

entries.name: Waxing
entries.summary: One of four phases used in the furstock birth table, applied separately to Masser and Secunda.

entries.name: New
entries.summary: One of four phases used in the furstock birth table, applied separately to Masser and Secunda.

entries.name: Waning
entries.summary: One of four phases used in the furstock birth table, applied separately to Masser and Secunda.

entries.name: Lunar Lattice (ja-Kha'jay)
entries.summary: The pattern woven by the moons' motion, believed to shield Mundus and to bind each Khajiit's form at birth.

entries.name: Elsweyr
entries.summary: Khajiit homeland in southern Tamriel: northern badlands and plains, southern jungles and river basins. A Third Empire province in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Annexed by Tiber Septim; Confederacy dissolved only in 4E 115

entries.name: Anequina
entries.summary: Arid northern half of Elsweyr, named for the warrior clan Ne Quin-al. Also an Oblivion Remastered Origin with the old male stat spread.
entries.eraNote: Half of the Elsweyr Confederacy (2E 309 to 4E 115); separate client state only from 4E 115

entries.name: Pellitine
entries.summary: Lush southern half of Elsweyr with jungles, rivers and beaches, rich from sugar and saltrice. Also an Oblivion Remastered Origin (old female stats).
entries.eraNote: Half of the Elsweyr Confederacy until 4E 115; spelled Pelletine in some sources

entries.name: High Savannah
entries.summary: Northern grassland of Anequina around Riverhold.

entries.name: The Scar
entries.summary: Great canyon of northern Elsweyr that winds around the mesa city of Orcrest.

entries.name: The Rim
entries.summary: Northeastern borderland near Cyrodiil whose chief city is Rimmen.

entries.name: Tenmar Forest
entries.summary: Southern jungle where moon sugar is native and where Torval stands.

entries.name: Quin'rawl Peninsula
entries.summary: Southeastern peninsula between Topal Bay and the Southern Sea, home of the port of Senchal.

entries.name: Khenarthi's Roost
entries.summary: Island in the Southern Sea shared by Khajiit and Maormer, with moon sugar plantations.
entries.eraNote: Geographic; most detail is from 2E sources

entries.name: Reaper's March
entries.summary: Contested borderland between Elsweyr and Valenwood, partly Khajiiti, near Dune.

entries.name: Trans-Niben (disputed)
entries.summary: Land between Elsweyr and Black Marsh handed back to County Leyawiin by the Mane ca. 3E 432; Khajiit radicals still claim it.
entries.eraNote: Mane and Empire agreement at the end of the Third Era

entries.name: Torval
entries.summary: Jungle city near Valenwood and seat of the Mane. An active city-state under King Mojtabe ca. 3E 389 to 399.
entries.eraNote: Listed as a capital on a ca. 3E 427 map

entries.name: Senchal
entries.summary: Huge southern port long known for pirates, thieves and skooma, later a resort for rich Khajiit. Had its own king in the late Third Era.
entries.eraNote: King Huskir ca. 3E 389 to 399; smuggler rumor dated 3E 432

entries.name: Rimmen
entries.summary: Walled resort city near the Cyrodiil border, often called Anequina's capital. Wealthy under King Ommed in the late Third Era.

entries.name: Dune
entries.summary: Hilltop merchant town by Reaper's March, home of the Temple of Two-Moons Dance where would-be Manes finish their path.
entries.eraNote: King Ab'ir in late 3E; war reached it in 3E 396

entries.name: Orcrest
entries.summary: Walled city perched on a plateau inside the Scar, reached by a large stone bridge.

entries.name: Riverhold
entries.summary: River crossroads and trading post on the northern border; Ta'agra name Rawla-Kei.
entries.eraNote: King Ab'dul in the late Third Era

entries.name: Corinthe
entries.summary: Highland city in the heart of the province at the edge of the Tenmar Forest, once an ancient kingdom.

entries.name: Ne Quin-al (old capital)
entries.summary: Former Anequinan capital with a Temple of Two-Moons Dance, taken by rebels in 2E 326. Use as ancestral flavor only.

entries.name: Northern nomads
entries.summary: Tribes and prides of the dry north who keep roaming ways; raiders sometimes rally under one chieftain.
entries.eraNote: Undated general description; consistent with Anequina Origin

entries.name: Southern city dwellers
entries.summary: Settled, mercantile southerners with a plantation aristocracy and strong arts, quick to adopt Imperial ways by the late Third Era.
entries.eraNote: Pellitine page: late Third Era description

entries.name: Ta'agra
entries.summary: Khajiiti language. Most natives also speak Tamrielic with their own dialect and drop Ta'agra words into it. 'Khajiit' roughly means desert-walker.

entries.name: Claw-Dances
entries.summary: Khajiiti unarmored martial arts, called Rain-of-Sand styles by outsiders, practiced as moving meditation in temples and adeptoriums.

entries.name: Moon sugar and skooma
entries.summary: Sacred crystal seen as solid moonlight, used as spice, ritual sacrament and drug. Illegal in the Third Empire and widely smuggled; skooma is its stronger form.

entries.name: Clan Mother
entries.summary: Matriarchs widely seen as the strongest force in Khajiit society because they control moon sugar harvest and refining.
entries.eraNote: Undated general description; 3E continuity assumed, not dated

entries.name: Moon-Singer
entries.summary: Respected lore-keepers and storytellers, mostly in Elsweyr; some tales are split across several singers to protect them.

entries.name: Cat Lord
entries.summary: Imperial nickname for the Mane.

entries.name: Forgotten Mane
entries.summary: Eclipse-born Khajiit not chosen as Mane, usually raised as warriors of the Pride of Alkosh.

entries.name: Elsweyr Confederacy
entries.summary: Union of Anequina and Pellitine formed by royal marriage, later absorbed as an Imperial province and dissolved by a Thalmor coup.

entries.name: Renrijra Krin
entries.summary: Khajiiti outlaws posing as freedom fighters, who want the Trans-Niben back and smuggle skooma; the Empire hunts them.
entries.eraNote: Bravil inquisitor set against them in 3E 433

entries.name: Baandari Pedlars
entries.summary: Wandering Khajiiti merchant clan, followers of Baan Dar under their own code, often suspected of theft. Also take non-Khajiit.
entries.eraNote: Only 2E 582 is dated on UESP; 3E presence unverified

entries.name: Pride of Alkosh
entries.summary: Warrior order of Alkosh trained at Pridehome, drawn from Forgotten Manes.

entries.name: Ne Quin-al clan
entries.summary: Ancient warrior clan skilled in war and tactics whose name became Anequina; kept nomadic customs in the north.
entries.eraNote: Pre-unification clan, after the 1E 2260 plague split

entries.name: Pa'alatiin clan
entries.summary: Ancient Moon-Priest clan that lived among all others and gave Pellitine its name; settled the south.

entries.name: Duneguard Outwalkers
entries.summary: Brigand clan, once the Dakarn Clan, that fought Valenwood's rangers in Reaper's March.
entries.eraNote: Active in the late Second Empire (late First Era)

entries.name: F'aashe
entries.summary: Free clan west of Rimmen whose warriors aided Attrebus Mede against Umbriel.

entries.name: Riddle'Thar (Two-Moons Dance)
entries.summary: Mainstream Khajiiti faith, more a code for living than one god, revealed by the prophet-Mane Rid-Thar-ri'Datta. Promises the paradise Llesw'er.

entries.name: Azurah
entries.summary: Mother of the Khajiit who bound them to the Lunar Lattice and made moon sugar. Khajiiti form of Azura, now seen as a distant mother.
entries.eraNote: Prominence fell after the Riddle'Thar but she is still revered

entries.name: Alkosh
entries.summary: Dragon King of Cats and god of time who keeps the moons moving. Folded into the Riddle'Thar but still popular in the wastelands.
entries.eraNote: Ongoing worship in the north per UESP

entries.name: Khenarthi
entries.summary: Sky and weather goddess, Khajiiti Kynareth. Carries the dead to Azurah or Llesw'er and guides sailors home.

entries.name: S'rendarr
entries.summary: The Runt, Khajiiti Stendarr, god of mercy, charity and justice.

entries.name: Rajhin
entries.summary: Thief god from Senchal's slums, patron of speed and slyness. Khajiit ask his blessing before unlawful work.
entries.eraNote: Undated; legend tied to Empress Kintyra

entries.name: Baan Dar
entries.summary: Bandit god of southern Tamriel, claimed by the Baandari as their patron.

entries.name: Jone and Jode
entries.summary: The Twin Lanterns, stillborn twins of Fadomai, whose light Azurah keeps lit. Their love reaches Khajiit through moonlight and moon sugar.

entries.name: Magrus
entries.summary: Khajiiti god of the sun and sorcery.

entries.name: Boethra
entries.summary: Patron of warriors and defiant exiles, who defeated Molagh in myth.

entries.name: Mafala
entries.summary: Keeper of hidden guilt whose worship faded after the Sinner Suicides.
entries.eraNote: Worship described as faded; no date

entries.name: Hircine
entries.summary: Hunt spirit said to guide lost Khajiit back to the Path.

entries.name: Lorkhaj
entries.summary: Khajiiti Lorkhan. His corrupted heart became the Moon Beast; most Khajiit now see him as a deceiver. Adversarial, not a normal faith pick.

entries.name: Namiira
entries.summary: The Great Darkness who drags fallen souls into the void as dro-m'Athra. Feared adversary, not a normal faith pick.

entries.name: Sheggorath
entries.summary: Khajiiti Sheogorath, blamed for the harmful side of skooma and moon sugar.

entries.name: Honorific rules
entries.summary: Names mostly describe a talent. One honorific at a time, set by status and changeable over life; wrong or doubled titles are insulting or arrogant.
entries.eraNote: Oblivion names use the system (J'zin-Dar, Ma'Raska)

entries.name: Dar / Daro
entries.summary: Oldest honorific: nimble-fingered, quick-tongued, clever. Female form Daro.

entries.name: Do
entries.summary: Martial master or renowned warrior, including guards of the Mane. Rarely taken by females.

entries.name: Dro / Dra
entries.summary: Elder, wise and witty; grandparent or head of family. Female form Dra.

entries.name: Ja (J')
entries.summary: Young adult, unmarried, still inexperienced. Often shortened to J'.

entries.name: Jo / Ko
entries.summary: Scholar, mage or healer, a graceful learned person. Female form Ko.

entries.name: La
entries.summary: Female-only honorific for a graceful unmarried maiden.

entries.name: Ma (M')
entries.summary: Child or apprentice, someone still learning. Often shortened to M'.

entries.name: Ra (R')
entries.summary: Leader in war, trade or government. Rarely taken by females.

entries.name: Ri
entries.summary: Chieftain, king, speaker or Mane; rarely granted. Should be locked or staff-approved on cards.

entries.name: Sa (S')
entries.summary: Plain adult. Not in the in-world references but common in names; often shortened to S'.

entries.name: Bynames and nicknames
entries.summary: Epithets like 'the Liar' or 'Iron-Ear' may attach to a name; plain nicknames never take an honorific. Family names are rare and not standard.

entries.name: Saxhleel (common Argonian)
entries.summary: The common reptilian Argonian seen across Tamriel; Saxhleel, 'People of the Root', is their own name and many dislike 'Argonian'.

entries.name: Agaceph
entries.summary: Inner-marsh breed with needle-shaped faces and vivid colors, using whip tails to steer rafts. Friendlier to outsiders than other inner tribes.

entries.name: Naga
entries.summary: Seven to eight foot breed with huge fanged mouths, prone to violence; many marsh brigands are tribeless Naga.
entries.eraNote: Attested across eras; undated as a breed

entries.name: Paatru
entries.summary: Toad-like breed of the inner swamps near the Hist, hostile to outsiders.

entries.name: Sarpa
entries.summary: Winged breed of the deep interior, said to kill outsiders.

entries.name: Hapsleet
entries.summary: Breed known only by name; differs in looks from common Argonians, details unknown.
entries.eraNote: Known to Second Era scholars; nothing later

entries.name: Marsh-born (Hist-bound)
entries.summary: Hatched in Black Marsh near a Hist, can hear it, and holds a Jel name from the naming rite.

entries.name: Lukiul
entries.summary: 'Assimilated': hatched outside Black Marsh or living among other races. Cannot hear the Hist and often misreads marsh-born body language.

entries.name: Black Marsh (Argonia)
entries.summary: Swamp province of southeastern Tamriel. Joined the Third Empire by treaty and was still a province in 3E 433; it broke away after the Crisis.
entries.eraNote: Secession only at the start of the Fourth Era

entries.name: Arnesia
entries.summary: Eastern region near Archon and Thorn, scarred by the Arnesian War with Morrowind; slavers still worked here. Also an Oblivion Remastered Origin.

entries.name: Thornmarsh
entries.summary: Temperate northeastern coast by Morrowind, called the Jewel of the East, main town Thorn. Also an Oblivion Remastered Origin.

entries.name: Shadowfen
entries.summary: Northern swamp region whose largest city is Stormhold.

entries.name: Murkmire
entries.summary: Southern swampland ending at the port of Lilmoth; home of many named tribes in older sources.

entries.name: Middle Argonia
entries.summary: Deep interior around Helstrom where the inner breeds live and outside armies rarely reach.

entries.name: Blackwood / Gloomire
entries.summary: Western marsh on the Leyawiin road, around Gideon.

entries.name: Topal Bay
entries.summary: Bay on the southwest coast, source of the Onkobra River, framed by Soulrest.

entries.name: Soulrest
entries.summary: Southwest coastal city that served as the Imperial capital of Black Marsh in the late Third Era.

entries.name: Helstrom
entries.summary: Interior city that many call the true Argonian capital; a full Imperial city-state in the Third Era.

entries.name: Stormhold
entries.summary: Largest city of Shadowfen on the Morrowind border, built over an Ayleid ruin, with an Imperial prison.

entries.name: Gideon
entries.summary: First town on the road from Leyawiin, built on a sunken Ayleid ruin; rival of Soulrest.

entries.name: Thorn
entries.summary: Northeastern city long raided and later ruled by House Dres slavers until 2E 572.

entries.name: Archon
entries.summary: East-coast city with a Shadowscale training ground, closed by 4E 187.
entries.eraNote: King Herula in the late Third Era

entries.name: Lilmoth
entries.summary: Stilted southern port run by merchant councils, with old Imperial ruins. Seized by the An-Xileel and ruined by Umbriel in the Fourth Era.
entries.eraNote: Queen Artomeda in late 3E; An-Xileel rule and Umbriel are 4E

entries.name: Blackrose
entries.summary: Murkmire settlement known for its Imperial-built prison.
entries.eraNote: Existence attested from 1E 1033; 3E status not dated

entries.name: The Hist
entries.summary: Sentient spore trees joined by one root mind. Their sap shapes hatchlings, gives names and visions, and souls return to them at death.
entries.eraNote: Hist foresaw and acted in the 3E 433 Crisis

entries.name: Sithis (Argonian view)
entries.summary: Revered as the force of change, not pure ruin. Argonians rebuild rather than mourn. Differs from the Dark Brotherhood's Sithis.

entries.name: Nisswo (Clutch of Nisswo)
entries.summary: Priests of Sithis, a loose coalition of preachers who gather each tribe's truths.

entries.name: Nisswo-King
entries.summary: Old priest-rulers who offered blood to a destructive Sithis and lost power at Duskfall. Ancestry flavor only.

entries.name: Shadowscales
entries.summary: Argonians born under The Shadow, given as infants to the Dark Brotherhood. Some return home as ku-vastei, agents of change.
entries.eraNote: Oblivion's Ocheeva and Teinaava are Shadowscales; extinct by ca. 4E 201

entries.name: Ku-vastei
entries.summary: Honor for Shadowscales who bring about needed change; tools of Sithis's will.

entries.name: Archein
entries.summary: Argonian tribe of hated kleptocrats who sold kin as slaves and served as advisors and rural governors under the Third Empire.
entries.eraNote: Third Empire governors; fate after the Crisis unknown

entries.name: An-Xileel
entries.summary: Hist-aligned nationalist party that rose in the Oblivion Crisis, called Argonians home and later expelled the Empire.
entries.eraNote: Formed during the 3E 433 Crisis; power is 4E. Allow only as nascent sympathizers

entries.name: Sul-Xan
entries.summary: Naga cult of Blackwood that worshipped Mehrunes Dagon and made sacrifices. Villain lore, not a player pick.

entries.name: Naga-Kur (Dead-Water)
entries.summary: Warlike Naga tribe of northern Murkmire that makes gear from its own dead.

entries.name: Bright-Throat (Wasseek-haleel)
entries.summary: Murkmire tribe of musicians, dancers and carvers who get on well with outsiders.

entries.name: Xit-Xaht
entries.summary: Fanatical warrior tribe of Mazzatun whose Hist clung to pre-Duskfall ways.

entries.name: Veeskhleel (Ghost People)
entries.summary: Pale-scaled Murkmire tribe that cannot lay eggs and steals them from others.

entries.name: Naka-Desh (Riverbacks)
entries.summary: Blackwood tribe seen as secretive, fond of riddles but not of cultural exchange.

entries.name: Veyond Cave tribe
entries.summary: Argonian tribesmen, shamans and a chieftain living in a cave in Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Chukka-Sei
entries.summary: Coming-of-age rite and naming day, when the young Argonian licks Hist sap and receives a Jel name.
entries.eraNote: Undated rite; Jel names appear in Oblivion

entries.name: Jel
entries.summary: Argonian language with only present-tense verbs. Outsiders are 'ojel', non-speakers, a neutral term.

entries.name: Grave-stake burial
entries.summary: The dead are staked into the mud with a xul-vaat; unstaked bodies may rise as bog blights.

entries.name: Jel name
entries.summary: Native name from the Hist at Chukka-Sei, often hyphenated roots, e.g. Haj-Ei, Geel, Mahei. Only marsh-born who pass the rite hold one.

entries.name: Tamrielic descriptive name
entries.summary: Phrase name in the common tongue, sometimes a literal Jel translation (Haj-Ei = Hides-His-Eyes), often about looks or deeds.

entries.name: Imperial-style name
entries.summary: Latin or Greek style given names (Julian, Demetrios, Athena) from Arena and Daggerfall naming tables.
entries.eraNote: Arena/Daggerfall era (3E 389 to 417); usage rules not stated

entries.name: Tribal titles
entries.summary: Tree-minder, sap-speaker, root-herald, kaal (war-captain), raj-kaal (war-chief), naheesh (elder), deelith (teacher).
entries.eraNote: Attested in Second Era sources; 3E use unverified

entries.name: Valenwood
entries.summary: Forested southwestern province of graht-oak canopy cities. Imperial province with a Camoran king pledged to the Empire since 3E 0.
entries.eraNote: Absorbed by Third Empire 3E 0; Thalmor coup only in 4E 29

entries.name: Grahtwood
entries.summary: Southeastern jungle of giant graht-oaks on the Padomaic coast, home of Elden Root. An Oblivion Remastered Origin for Wood Elves.
entries.eraNote: Listed as Wood Elf Origin in Oblivion Remastered (3E 433)

entries.name: Reaper's March
entries.summary: Thinly wooded northeastern borderland facing Cyrodiil and Elsweyr, often raided by Colovians and Khajiit. An Oblivion Remastered Origin.
entries.eraNote: Listed as Wood Elf Origin in Oblivion Remastered (3E 433)

entries.name: Greenshade
entries.summary: Southwestern woodland of meadows and clearings, rich in sacred sites. Main city Woodhearth.
entries.eraNote: Geography; name attested mostly in 2E (ESO) sources, no rename recorded

entries.name: Malabal Tor
entries.summary: Dense northwestern jungle holding the holy city of Silvenar. Wood Orc clans also live along its coast.
entries.eraNote: Geography; name attested mostly in 2E (ESO) sources, no rename recorded

entries.name: Falinesti
entries.summary: The walking city: a giant tree that moved between four seasonal sites and was the old Camoran seat. It finally put down roots near the end of the Third Era.
entries.eraNote: Rooted in 'twilight years' of 3E, exact year and site unknown; King Elisgorn c. 3E 389-399

entries.name: Elden Root (Eldenroot)
entries.summary: Grahtwood's capital, grown in and around a colossal Elden Tree, with markets in the trunk and an underworld in the caves below.
entries.eraNote: Ruled by Queen Ulandra in late 3E (3E 389-399 era)

entries.name: Silvenar
entries.summary: Spiritual heart of Valenwood on the Xylo River, seat of the Silvenar and the Green Lady. A city-state under King Paligorn in the late Third Era.

entries.name: Woodhearth
entries.summary: Chief city of Greenshade on its western tip.
entries.eraNote: No destruction or abandonment recorded before 4E; 3E attestation not checked directly

entries.name: Arenthia
entries.summary: Mixed-culture border city of Reaper's March near Cyrodiil and Elsweyr. Rival of Silvenar in the late Third Era.
entries.eraNote: Named as Silvenar's rival in late 3E (3E 389-399 era)

entries.name: Southpoint
entries.summary: Imperial-founded harbor in southwestern Grahtwood. Rival of Elden Root in the late Third Era.
entries.eraNote: Named as Elden Root's rival in late 3E

entries.name: Greenheart
entries.summary: Southern Greenshade city close to the sea. Rival of Elden Root in the late Third Era.
entries.eraNote: Named as Elden Root's rival in late 3E

entries.name: Haven
entries.summary: Altmer-built port on the southeastern Grahtwood shore.

entries.name: Green Pact Bosmer (tribal / strict)
entries.summary: Wood Elves who keep the Pact strictly: eat only meat, never harm living Valenwood plants, never take beast form. Most common in remote villages.
entries.eraNote: Pact observance ongoing; no end date recorded

entries.name: Civilized (urban) Bosmer
entries.summary: Town and city Wood Elves who follow the Pact more loosely, yet still tend to defend its principles. Fits Bosmer living in Cyrodiil.
entries.eraNote: Described without date as an ongoing divide

entries.name: Apostate (Pact-breaker)
entries.summary: A Bosmer who has broken the Green Pact. Believed to be cast into the Ooze after death. A heavy stigma, good for exile backstories.
entries.eraNote: Concept ongoing in sources; no dated end

entries.name: Oathbreakers
entries.summary: Ancient sect of Bosmer who refused the Pact and were subdued and buried in the Ooze. Some escaped and became Changelings. Legend, not a living group.

entries.name: 'Salad-eater' (slur)
entries.summary: Mocking label Pact loyalists use for Bosmer who ignore the Pact's food rules. Useful RP insult, not a formal group.
entries.eraNote: Undated slur from the Pact schism

entries.name: Ayleid-descended
entries.summary: Lines tracing back to Ayleid refugees who fled Cyrodiil and were let into Valenwood on condition of taking the Pact.
entries.eraNote: Ayleid Diaspora after 1E 243; valid only as ancestry

entries.name: Camoran line
entries.summary: Royal dynasty founded by Eplear at the dawn of the First Era. Carries a dark stain in 3E 433: Mankar Camoran, son of the Usurper, leads the Mythic Dawn.
entries.eraNote: Camoran kings ruled under the Empire from 3E 0; Usurper 3E 249-267

entries.name: Green Pact (Treaty of Frond and Leaf)
entries.summary: Y'ffre's covenant: guard the forest, eat only meat, waste nothing, eat slain foes within three days, keep the form Y'ffre gave. Fallen fruit and honey are usually fine.
entries.eraNote: Ongoing; Meat Mandate rare outside remote villages since 2E

entries.name: Meat Mandate
entries.summary: The Pact rule that fallen enemies must be eaten, not left to rot. By the Second Era mostly kept only by zealous, remote villages.

entries.name: Matrilineal clans
entries.summary: At clan level Bosmer society traces descent through mothers. Clans judge Pact crimes and can hand the guilty over to the Green.

entries.name: Wild Hunt
entries.summary: Desperate group ritual turning Bosmer into a horde of shapeless beasts, permanently. Rarely spoken of. Last documented case 3E 397 at Vindisi.
entries.eraNote: 3E 397 Vindisi; possibly near Falinesti c. 3E 433 (sources conflict)

entries.name: Rite of Theft
entries.summary: Custom where one Bosmer steals from another and asks a favor in exchange for returning the item.

entries.name: Y'ffre
entries.summary: Chief Bosmer god: the Storyteller, god of song and forest, who gave things lasting names and forms and set up the Green Pact.

entries.name: Bosmeri Eight
entries.summary: Y'ffre, Auri-El (little honored), Arkay, Xarxes, Mara, Stendarr, Z'en and Baan Dar. Hircine and the Wilderking also loom in folk belief.

entries.name: The Ooze
entries.summary: The formless chaos before Y'ffre named the world. Pact-breakers are said to return to it after death.

entries.name: The Silvenar
entries.summary: Spiritual Voice of the People who embodies the Pact. Chosen by the Green, not by vote. Not a player title.

entries.name: The Green Lady
entries.summary: The Silvenar's partner and the physical face of the people, bound to the Silvenar in the generational Handfasting. Not a player title.

entries.name: Treethane
entries.summary: Local Bosmer leader with widely varying authority, part of Valenwood's loose patchwork rule. Some enforce the Pact.
entries.eraNote: Described as current office in Lore:Y'ffre; mostly 2E examples

entries.name: Spinner
entries.summary: Priest of Y'ffre who keeps stories and laws and enforces the Pact. Often said to hold the real power in Valenwood.

entries.name: Jaqspur
entries.summary: Earned title for elite long-range archers with a fast snatch-and-release draw. Work as scouts, trackers, hunters and guards.
entries.eraNote: Lady Allena Benoch was a Third Era Jaqspur

entries.name: Silvenar's Own Jaqspurs
entries.summary: Elite personal guard of the Silvenar, disbanded before the mid-Second Era and revived under the first Aldmeri Dominion.

entries.name: Camoran Usurper's host
entries.summary: Haymon Camoran's army of mercenaries and Daedra that ravaged Valenwood and marched on High Rock until his death.

entries.name: Aldmeri Dominion (Bosmer member)
entries.summary: Valenwood joined the first Dominion in 2E 580 and was forced into the second in 2E 830. Not a current allegiance in 3E 433.

entries.name: Bosmer given names
entries.summary: Usually one given name, e.g. Glarthir, Thurindil, Carwen, Nilawen. Older games built them from prefix plus suffix (Elis-las, Min-thia).

entries.name: Bosmer family names
entries.summary: Most Bosmer have no surname. Rare ones are nature compounds (Willowwood, Bluebrook) or clan names such as Camoran, Rayn, Oreyn.

entries.name: Bosmer bynames
entries.summary: Epithets from deeds or looks: 'the Shepherd', Arrow-Catcher, Two-Scars. Often used in place of a surname.

entries.name: Imga (not Bosmer)
entries.summary: Great Apes of Valenwood who share the land with the Bosmer. A separate beast people, listed here only to exclude it.
entries.eraNote: Existing people, not a Bosmer subtype

entries.name: Summerset Isles
entries.summary: Archipelago of fourteen islands southwest of Tamriel. An Imperial province since Tiber Septim's conquest, under the Altmeri monarchy at Alinor.

entries.name: Summerset Isle
entries.summary: Largest island, holding Alinor, Lillandril, Shimmerene, Dusk, Sunhold and Cloudrest. An Oblivion Remastered Origin.
entries.eraNote: Listed as High Elf Origin in Oblivion Remastered (3E 433)

entries.name: Auridon
entries.summary: Second island, nearest the mainland, with Firsthold and Skywatch. Traditional Aldmer landfall. An Oblivion Remastered Origin.
entries.eraNote: Listed as High Elf Origin in Oblivion Remastered (3E 433)

entries.name: Artaeum
entries.summary: Psijic Order island that can vanish from the world for centuries. Only fits a Psijic-linked character.
entries.eraNote: Present per Psijic timeline until early 4E vanishing; sources conflict

entries.name: Alinor (city)
entries.summary: Capital on the west shore of Summerset Isle and seat of the Altmeri crown.

entries.name: Firsthold
entries.summary: Oldest Altmer city, on northern Auridon. In the Third Era ruled for a time by the Dunmer Queen Morgiah.

entries.name: Skywatch
entries.summary: Central Auridon city with its own king in the Third Era.
entries.eraNote: Lady Gialene, daughter of Skywatch's king, in 3E

entries.name: Cloudrest
entries.summary: City perched on Eton Nir, tallest peak of the Isles.
entries.eraNote: No destruction recorded; 3E attestation not checked directly

entries.name: Shimmerene
entries.summary: City in east-central Summerset Isle.
entries.eraNote: No destruction recorded; 3E attestation not checked directly

entries.name: Lillandril
entries.summary: Northwestern city near the College of Sapiarchs. Known for friction with the Mages Guild.
entries.eraNote: No destruction recorded; 3E attestation not checked directly

entries.name: Dusk
entries.summary: City on the southeastern coast of Summerset Isle.
entries.eraNote: No destruction recorded; 3E attestation not checked directly

entries.name: Sunhold
entries.summary: City in the south-southwest of Summerset Isle.
entries.eraNote: No destruction recorded; 3E attestation not checked directly

entries.name: Crystal Tower
entries.summary: Ancient symbol of Altmer learning. During the Oblivion Crisis it sheltered refugees until Daedric forces brought it down.

entries.name: Alinor (as province name)
entries.summary: Thalmor-era name for the whole Summerset province. Do not use for a 3E 433 character.

entries.name: Altmer class hierarchy
entries.summary: Rigid order grown over millennia: the Wise on top, then Artists, Princes, Warriors, Landowners, Merchants, Workers.

entries.name: Lineage and bloodline prestige
entries.summary: Standing rests on lineage and speech. Full names can record both parents' lines; purity of royal blood is a political issue.

entries.name: Resentment of Talos
entries.summary: Many Altmer quietly resent Tiber Septim's deification, remembering his conquest of Summerset. Good RP friction with Imperials.
entries.eraNote: Third Era, after the Third Empire's founding

entries.name: Hulkynd
entries.summary: Infants judged deformed or impure, often abandoned. Some are raised by priests of Stendarr. A grim outcast backstory.

entries.name: Calian
entries.summary: Aetherquartz sphere given at coming of age as a token of honor; shattering it marks an outcast (apraxic).

entries.name: Aldmeri pantheon
entries.summary: Ancestor-gods led by Auri-El: Magnus, Trinimac, Jephre, Xarxes, Mara, Stendarr, Syrabane, plus Phynaster. Traditionalists reject a fixed count of Eight.

entries.name: Auri-El
entries.summary: Chief Aldmeri god, seen by the Altmer as their literal ancestor.

entries.name: Trinimac
entries.summary: Auri-El's champion knight. Myth says Boethiah devoured him and he became Malacath; Altmer still honor him as their shield.
entries.eraNote: Honored by Altmer; Orc Trinimac cult c. 3E 399

entries.name: Magnus
entries.summary: God of magic in the Aldmeri Eight.

entries.name: Syrabane
entries.summary: Aldmeri patron of mages and warlocks, credited with helping stop the Thrassian Plague. Favored by younger Mages Guild members.

entries.name: Phynaster
entries.summary: Summerset hero-god, the Guardian, said to have taught the Altmer to gain about a century of life by shortening their stride.

entries.name: Xarxes
entries.summary: Keeper of Aldmeri deeds and lineages; ties into Altmer ancestor reverence.

entries.name: Psijic Order
entries.summary: Ancient monastic order on Artaeum keeping the Old Ways. Mostly Altmer, very selective, with centuries-long apprenticeships. Rare, admin-gated pick.
entries.eraNote: 30 initiates 3E 430-432 per Lore:Psijic_Order; Lore:Altmer says gone after 3E 110 (conflict)

entries.name: Thalmor (Dominion-era council)
entries.summary: Originally a bureau guarding Altmer heritage, later executive arm of the first and second Dominions and ruler of Valenwood.
entries.eraNote: 2E 580 and 2E 830; dissolved when Tiber Septim took Valenwood

entries.name: Thalmor (late Third Era movement)
entries.summary: Fringe supremacist movement, ignored for years and not in power in 3E 433. Sources disagree whether it existed before or only after the Crisis.
entries.eraNote: Lore:Thalmor: resurfaced 'sometime prior' to 3E 433; Lore:Altmer: name taken after the Crisis

entries.name: First Aldmeri Dominion
entries.summary: Queen Ayrenn's alliance of Summerset, Valenwood and Elsweyr during the Three Banners War. Ancestry flavor only.

entries.name: Second Aldmeri Dominion
entries.summary: Summerset's union with a conquered Valenwood, ended by Tiber Septim's conquest.

entries.name: Third Aldmeri Dominion
entries.summary: Thalmor-led union of Alinor and Valenwood that later wars with the Empire. Not available in 3E 433.

entries.name: Veiled Heritance
entries.summary: Secret society that wanted every non-Altmer expelled from Summerset and tried to kill Queen Ayrenn.

entries.name: Altmeri monarch
entries.summary: Summerset's crown at Alinor, under Imperial rule in 3E 433. City kings such as Skywatch's also exist. Not a player title.

entries.name: Sapiarch
entries.summary: Scholar of the College of Sapiarchs; each studies one field and they tutor royal heirs.

entries.name: Kinlord / Kinlady
entries.summary: Altmer noble title over a family line and its holdings.
entries.eraNote: Attested only in 2E (ESO) sources; 3E use unverified

entries.name: Canonreeve
entries.summary: Altmer civil office, roughly a magistrate. Related titles: vicereeve, jurisreeve.
entries.eraNote: Attested only in 2E (ESO) sources; 3E use unverified

entries.name: Clan Direnni
entries.summary: Merchant-noble Altmer clan from Tyrigel that held the Adamantine Tower and once ruled High Rock. Ancestors of the Bretons on their elven side.

entries.name: Clan Corelanya
entries.summary: Clan descended from followers of Veloth who revere the Three Queens (Meridia, Azura, Nocturnal). Daedra worship is outlawed in Summerset.

entries.name: Altmer given names
entries.summary: Single elegant given names, e.g. Erissare, Elante. Older games used prefix plus suffix patterns.

entries.name: Altmer family names
entries.summary: Surnames exist but are seldom shown. Examples: Direnni, Rilis, Camoran. Often swapped for 'of <city>', e.g. Elante of Alinor.

entries.name: Morrowind
entries.summary: Volcanic northeastern province. Imperial since the Armistice but self-ruling under King Helseth and the Great Houses.
entries.eraNote: Armistice after 2E 882; Imperial until early 4E (not Imperial by 4E 48)

entries.name: Vvardenfell
entries.summary: Island district around Red Mountain, opened to settlers in 3E 414 and hit by the Blight until 3E 427. An Oblivion Remastered Origin.
entries.eraNote: Listed as Dark Elf Origin in Oblivion Remastered; Red Year 4E 5 is future

entries.name: Mainland Morrowind
entries.summary: Everything outside Vvardenfell: Deshaan, Stonefalls, Dres south, Telvanni peninsula. An Oblivion Remastered Origin.
entries.eraNote: Listed as Dark Elf Origin in Oblivion Remastered (3E 433)

entries.name: Deshaan
entries.summary: Fertile southern plain around Mournhold, Indoril heartland.

entries.name: Stonefalls
entries.summary: Western mainland on the Inner Sea's southwest shore, with Ebonheart and Kragenmoor.

entries.name: Telvanni Peninsula
entries.summary: East-central coast (Fungal Lowlands, Padomaic Crest) and nearby isles, home of the Telvanni wizard-lords.

entries.name: Southern Morrowind (Dres lands)
