entries.summary: Plantation country bordering Black Marsh, seat of House Dres at Tear.

entries.name: Ashlands and West Gash
entries.summary: Ash-blown north and west of Vvardenfell, range of the Urshilaku tribe.

entries.name: Grazelands
entries.summary: Eastern Vvardenfell grassland, range of the Zainab tribe.

entries.name: Molag Amur
entries.summary: Harsh volcanic badlands, range of the Erabenimsun tribe.

entries.name: Azura's Coast
entries.summary: Eastern Vvardenfell shore, range of the Ahemmusa tribe.

entries.name: Solstheim (as Morrowind land)
entries.summary: Northern island granted to Morrowind after the Red Year. Not Dunmer territory in 3E 433.

entries.name: Mournhold
entries.summary: Indoril city and capital of Morrowind, seat of King Helseth, inside the larger city of Almalexia.

entries.name: Vivec City
entries.summary: Temple city of great cantons on Vvardenfell's south coast. Its later destruction is future.

entries.name: Balmora
entries.summary: Hlaalu council seat on the Odai River, busiest Imperial-friendly town of Vvardenfell.

entries.name: Ald'ruhn
entries.summary: Redoran council seat west of Red Mountain. Its citadel was destroyed during the Oblivion Crisis: a strong RP hook.
entries.eraNote: Citadel destroyed in the Oblivion Crisis, 3E 433

entries.name: Sadrith Mora
entries.summary: Telvanni council seat in the eastern islands, full of mushroom towers.

entries.name: Port Telvannis
entries.summary: Northeastern Telvanni capital where the Parliament of Bugs meets.

entries.name: Necrom
entries.summary: Eastern coastal city of the dead and Temple burial grounds.

entries.name: Narsis
entries.summary: Ancient Hlaalu capital in the southwest mainland.

entries.name: Tear
entries.summary: Dres capital on the southeast coast near Black Marsh.

entries.name: Ebonheart
entries.summary: City whose castle on Vvardenfell housed the Imperial Duke and the Grand Council in the late Third Era.
entries.eraNote: Castle Ebonheart seat of Duke and Council, late 3E

entries.name: Blacklight
entries.summary: Redoran stronghold in the northwest; becomes Morrowind's capital only after the Red Year.

entries.name: Cheydinhal (Cyrodiil)
entries.summary: Eastern Cyrodiil town with Dunmer-style architecture and a Dunmer Count, Andel Indarys. Main home of Dark Elves in Cyrodiil.
entries.eraNote: Count since before 3E 433; Dunmer emigration c. 3E 433

entries.name: House Dunmer (settled)
entries.summary: Dark Elves of the towns and plantations, sworn to or living under a Great House and the Temple.

entries.name: Ashlander
entries.summary: Nomadic Dunmer of the wastes who keep the old ancestor and Daedra faith and reject the Tribunal. Wary of outlanders.

entries.name: Velothi
entries.summary: Ashlander-descended Dunmer who settled among the Great Houses.

entries.name: Cyrodiil Dunmer (diaspora)
entries.summary: Dark Elves living in Cyrodiil, centered on Cheydinhal, an early wave of the Dunmer diaspora.

entries.name: Chimer ancestry
entries.summary: Golden-skinned forebears who left Summerset with Veloth and were cursed by Azura into Dunmer after Red Mountain. Ancestry only.
entries.eraNote: Curse at Battle of Red Mountain, 1E 700

entries.name: House Redoran
entries.summary: Warrior house of duty and honor, seated at Ald'ruhn and the most powerful house of recent centuries. Supplies many Buoyant Armigers.

entries.name: House Hlaalu
entries.summary: Merchant house friendliest to the Empire, seated at Balmora, leading under King Helseth. Tainted by Camonna Tong links.
entries.eraNote: Leading house late 3E; loses status early 4E

entries.name: House Telvanni
entries.summary: Isolationist wizard-lords in mushroom towers, seated at Sadrith Mora and Port Telvannis. Power through magic, little law.

entries.name: House Indoril
entries.summary: Orthodox house bound to the Temple and hostile to the Empire, holding Mournhold. Lost its lead on the Council at the Armistice.

entries.name: House Dres
entries.summary: Agrarian slaver house of the south, seated at Tear. Clung to slavery long after others moved on.
entries.eraNote: Active Great House late 3E; slavery banned by Helseth late 3E

entries.name: House Dagoth (Sixth House)
entries.summary: Lost house destroyed after Red Mountain; its lord Dagoth Ur fell in 3E 427. Membership in 3E 433 means a hunted cultist.

entries.name: House Sadras
entries.summary: Takes Hlaalu's Council seat after the Red Year. Not a Great House in 3E 433.

entries.name: Great House ranks
entries.summary: Hlaalu/Redoran: Hireling, Retainer, Oathman, Lawman, Kinsman, House Cousin, House Brother, House Father, Councilman. Telvanni: Mouth, Spellwright, Wizard, Master, Magister.

entries.name: Councilor / Hortator
entries.summary: House councilors sit on the Grand Council; in grave danger they may elect a Hortator as war leader.

entries.name: Archmagister / Archmaster / Grandmaster
entries.summary: Top ranks of Telvanni, Redoran and Hlaalu respectively. Not a player title.

entries.name: King of Morrowind
entries.summary: Helseth reigns from Mournhold under the Empire and banned slavery late in the era. Not a player title.

entries.name: Urshilaku
entries.summary: Ashlander tribe of the Ashlands and West Gash, most devoted to the Nerevarine prophecies.

entries.name: Ahemmusa
entries.summary: Ashlander tribe of Azura's Coast.

entries.name: Erabenimsun
entries.summary: Ashlander tribe of Molag Amur.

entries.name: Zainab
entries.summary: Ashlander tribe of the Grazelands.

entries.name: Mainland tribes (Kagesh, Ulath, Vereansu)
entries.summary: Ashlander tribes of Stonefalls and Deshaan.

entries.name: Mabrigash
entries.summary: Ashlander witch-warrior cult of the Ghost Snake, founded by Farseer Hareth.
entries.eraNote: First Era origin; later status unverified

entries.name: Ashkhan
entries.summary: Chief of an Ashlander tribe.

entries.name: Wise Woman / Farseer
entries.summary: Tribal seer who reads dreams as prophecy. A Farseer is her apprentice. Gulakhan is the Ashkhan's war leader rank.

entries.name: Clanfriend
entries.summary: Outsider adopted by a tribe for good deeds. Lets non-Ashlander Dunmer claim tribal ties.

entries.name: Tribunal Temple
entries.summary: State church of Almalexia, Sotha Sil and Vivec (ALMSIVI). In 3E 433 shaken: the gods lost their divine source in 3E 427 and are dead or missing.
entries.eraNote: Tribunal falls late 3E; New Temple is later

entries.name: Ancestor worship
entries.summary: Core of all Dunmer religion: family spirits guard the household and tomb. Daedra are counted as ancestors too.

entries.name: Good Daedra (Azura, Boethiah, Mephala)
entries.summary: The Chimer's old gods. Under the Temple called the Anticipations; Ashlanders worship them directly.
entries.eraNote: Ongoing; 'Reclamations' name is New Temple era

entries.name: House of Troubles
entries.summary: Mehrunes Dagon, Sheogorath, Malacath and Molag Bal, seen as gods who test the Dunmer.

entries.name: Nerevarine cult
entries.summary: Urshilaku-rooted belief in Nerevar reborn as an outlander. The prophecy was fulfilled in 3E 427.

entries.name: New Temple (Reclamations)
entries.summary: Reformed faith that returns to Azura, Boethiah and Mephala after the Tribunal. Not established in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Formed after the Red Year (4E); Lore:Dunmer is vague

entries.name: Ordinators
entries.summary: Temple guards and holy soldiers, dominated by House Indoril.

entries.name: Buoyant Armigers
entries.summary: Vivec's knights, mostly Redoran, who guarded the Ghostfence and shrines.

entries.name: Dissident Priests
entries.summary: Secret dissenters inside the Temple; they later become the New Temple.

entries.name: Morag Tong
entries.summary: Mephala-worshipping assassins' guild licensed to carry out legal writs in Morrowind. Bitter rival of the Dark Brotherhood.

entries.name: Camonna Tong
entries.summary: Anti-outlander Dunmer crime syndicate tied to House Hlaalu. Members were seen in Cyrodiil in 3E 433 dealing skooma with Cheydinhal's Orum gang.

entries.name: Slavery
entries.summary: Long protected Dunmer custom targeting Argonians and Khajiit, banned by King Helseth late in the Third Era amid violent backlash.

entries.name: Dunmer names
entries.summary: Given name plus family name, e.g. Dranas Lerano, Fathis Aren, Andel Indarys. Some families share a Great House name (Balen Hlaalu).

entries.name: Ashlander names
entries.summary: UESP keeps separate Ashlander given- and family-name lists; Ashlanders do carry family names.

entries.name: Orsinium (Nova Orsinium)
entries.summary: Third Orc kingdom founded by Gortwog gro-Nagorm in High Rock between Menevia and Wayrest. An Oblivion Remastered Origin.

entries.name: Stronghold
entries.summary: Walled clan settlement in the mountains, ruled by a chief under the Code of Malacath. An Oblivion Remastered Origin.
entries.eraNote: Listed as Orc Origin in Oblivion Remastered (3E 433)

entries.name: Wrothgarian Mountains (Wrothgar)
entries.summary: Mountains between High Rock and Skyrim, site of the first two Orsiniums and home of Wrothgarian Orc clans.
entries.eraNote: Geography; old Orsinium sites are historical

entries.name: Dragontail Mountains
entries.summary: Mountains of Hammerfell's east; Iron Orc range. Thulgeg's horde crossed them in 1E 874.

entries.name: Old Orsinium
entries.summary: First Orsinium, besieged from 1E 950 and razed in 1E 980; Kurog's second city in east Wrothgar in the Second Era.

entries.name: Stronghold Orc
entries.summary: Orc raised inside a clan stronghold under a chief and the unwritten Code.

entries.name: City Orc
entries.summary: Orc living outside the strongholds, often Legion-trained or a hired hand. Stronghold Orcs use the name as an insult.
entries.eraNote: Ongoing; many Orcs in Oblivion's Cyrodiil

entries.name: Wood Orc
entries.summary: Valenwood Orcs, nimble like Bosmer but not bound by the Green Pact; they sell metal, coal and wood to the Bosmer and honor Mauloch.
entries.eraNote: Cited in Pocket Guide 3E 432; main history 1E-2E

entries.name: Mountain Orc
entries.summary: Orcs of the hills of northern Morrowind, counted as Dunmer enemies. Includes the isolated, tough Malahk-Orcs.

entries.name: Iron Orc (Osh Ornim)
entries.summary: Dragontail and Craglorn Orcs known for stone worship, iron gear, alchemy and taming trolls and wamasu.

entries.name: Desert Orc
entries.summary: Alik'r desert clans led by Thulgeg, driven out of Hammerfell to Wrothgar.

entries.name: Code of Malacath
entries.summary: Unwritten stronghold law: honor demands vengeance, crimes are paid off with a blood price, and the strongest takes the chief's seat by combat.

entries.name: Legion service
entries.summary: Many Third Era Orcs gained schooling and slow acceptance through the Imperial Legion. Tiber Septim had refused them citizenship.
entries.eraNote: Late 3E; no exact date or emperor named

entries.name: Marriage alliances
entries.summary: Clan daughters are often married into other strongholds to bind alliances.

entries.name: Chief
entries.summary: Head of a stronghold, usually the strongest male, replaced when a challenger kills him.

entries.name: Wise-Woman
entries.summary: Recognized stronghold role alongside the chief. Also used as a name prefix: Wise-Woman Ushuta.

entries.name: Forge-wife / Hearth-wife / Shield-wife
entries.summary: Named roles among a chief's wives (huntswife, forgewife, hearthwife, shieldwife). Usable as a card role for female stronghold Orcs.

entries.name: King of Orsinium
entries.summary: Gortwog gro-Nagorm won the land in a duel and forced Uriel VII to recognize Orsinium. Ruler in 3E 433 not confirmed.

entries.name: Malacath (Mauloch)
entries.summary: Daedric Prince of outcasts, oaths and curses, patron and 'Orc-Father' of the Orsimer.

entries.name: Trinimac cult
entries.summary: Orcs who hold that Trinimac still lives and Malacath is a deceiver. Gortwog founded a priesthood; most Orcs call it heresy.

entries.name: Orc clans
entries.summary: Clans such as Fharun, Igrun, Morkul, Bagrakh, Shatul. The clan or stronghold of birth becomes the family name.
entries.eraNote: Clan names attested across eras; specific clans' 3E status unverified

entries.name: gro- / gra- family names
entries.summary: Given name plus gro- (male) or gra- (female) and the clan or stronghold of birth: Agronak gro-Malog, Borba gra-Uzgash.

entries.name: Orc role prefixes and epithets
entries.summary: Role titles go before the name (Chief Ulukhaz, Hearth-Wife Sholg); epithets after it (the Iron Hand, Axe-Hands).

entries.name: Orsimer ('Pariah Folk')
entries.summary: Aldmeri name meaning cursed or outcast folk, from Trinimac's followers. Orcs call themselves Ornim; Orsinium means Orc-Town.

entries.name: Skyrim strongholds (Dushnikh Yal, Largashbur, Mor Khazgur, Narzulbur)
entries.summary: Orc strongholds known from 4E 201 Skyrim. Existence in 3E 433 unverified, so not offered as a birthplace.

entries.name: Dra'bul
entries.summary: Largest Wood Orc stronghold, on the north coast of Malabal Tor, seat of Clan Drublog.

entries.name: Hammerfell
entries.summary: Western desert-and-coast province settled by Yokudan colonists in the First Era. A Septim Empire province in 3E 433, split between Crown and Forebear politics.
entries.eraNote: Imperial province since 2E 864; independence only after the Great War (4E 175+).

entries.name: Crowns
entries.summary: Traditionalist Redguards descended from the Yokudan royal class. Keep the old Yokudan gods, distrust outsiders and Imperial ways. Strongest inland and in the south.
entries.eraNote: Active party in the 3E 432 Pocket Guide; Ayaan-si of Elinhir urges Crowns to revolt ca. 3E 433. Reconciled with Forebears only in the Great War (4E).

entries.name: Forebears
entries.summary: Cosmopolitan Redguards descended from the Ra Gada warrior wave. Traders and city folk who embraced the Septim Empire and largely worship the Divines.
entries.eraNote: Embraced Tiber Septim's Empire in 3E; Sentinel under the Forebear King Lhotun in 3E 432.

entries.name: Lhotunics
entries.summary: Middle-ground movement named for King Lhotun of Sentinel. Honors Yokudan heritage while accepting Imperial customs; scorned by both Crowns and Forebears.
entries.eraNote: Late Third Era; described as current in the 3E 432 Pocket Guide.

entries.name: Alik'r nomads
entries.summary: Desert tribes of the Alik'r, of Yokudan or older Nedic stock. Known as wanderers and hired swords; hold Satakal in high regard.
entries.eraNote: Described as a standing population of the Alik'r; no end date in UESP.

entries.name: Satakals (desert worshippers)
entries.summary: Roaming Satakal devotees of the deep desert, respected for charity but feared as raiders. The Third Empire barred them from the cities.
entries.eraNote: Third Empire ban on entering cities implies 3E presence; 3E 432 guide notes Satakal worship called heresy by Queen Clavilla.

entries.name: Ash'abah
entries.summary: Pariah desert tribe from Yath who fight the restless dead; shunned for handling corpses, which most Redguards hold sacred. Some Forebears help them.
entries.eraNote: Best attested in 2E 582 (ESO). 3E 433 presence not documented on the pages read: unverified, treat as ancestry only until checked.

entries.name: Ra Gada descent
entries.summary: The Yokudan Warrior Wave that conquered Hammerfell around 1E 808. Forebears claim descent from them; usable as proud ancestry.

entries.name: Na-Totambu descent
entries.summary: The old Yokudan royal line and government that followed the Ra Gada to Tamriel. Crowns trace their lineage to it.
entries.eraNote: First Era Yokudan royalty; no Na-Totambu court exists in 3E 433.

entries.name: Yokudan
entries.summary: The people of lost Yokuda, ancestors of all Redguards. A living 'pure Yokudan' in 3E 433 is not possible; use only as ancestry flavor.
entries.eraNote: Yokuda sank before/around the First Era migration (1E 808 landing).

entries.name: Sword-singers
entries.summary: Yokudan warrior-mystics of the Way of the Sword, said to summon spirit blades. Their tradition shapes Redguard swordplay; no organized order in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: First Era (War of the Singers ca. 1E 780).

entries.name: Ansei (Sword Saint)
entries.summary: Honorific for the greatest sword-singers; Frandar and Divad Hunding are the famous examples. Legendary, not a rank a 3E character holds.
entries.eraNote: First Era; no 3E bearers documented on the pages read.

entries.name: Gallants of Hammerfell
entries.summary: Desert knights skilled with sword and Yokudan charger, also called Knights of the Desert.
entries.eraNote: Undated on Lore:Alik'r; 3E 433 status unverified. Defaulted to historical pending review.

entries.name: Alik'r Desert
entries.summary: Vast west-central sand sea, home of nomad tribes and Crown strongholds. Sentinel sits on its northwest edge.
entries.eraNote: Geography; Alik'r kingdoms became Imperial vassals after 3E 417.

entries.name: Craglorn
entries.summary: Northeastern highlands below the Dragontails holding Elinhir and Dragonstar; contested with Skyrim since the Bend'r-mahk war.
entries.eraNote: Skyrim claimed Elinhir's territory and split Dragonstar in 3E 397.

entries.name: Dragontail Mountains
entries.summary: Northern range dividing eastern and western Hammerfell; HoonDing survives there as a local spirit.

entries.name: Khefrem
entries.summary: Southwest coastal region containing Gilane and Hew's Bane.
entries.eraNote: Geography; region name is mostly from ESO-era sources.

entries.name: Sunforge
entries.summary: Hot central region around Skaven.

entries.name: Iliac Bay coast (Kingdom of Sentinel)
entries.summary: Northern Hammerfell coast united under Sentinel by the Warp in the West: Abibon-Gora, Bergama, Lainlyn, Satakalaam and more.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries.summary: Forebear capital and the strongest Iliac Bay kingdom after 3E 417, ruled by King Lhotun. Founded by Grandee Yaghoub's Ra Gada.

entries.name: Rihad
entries.summary: Forebear stronghold city in southern Hammerfell.
entries.eraNote: Forebear city through the Third Era (fought the Camoran Usurper, 3E 253).

entries.name: Taneth
entries.summary: Forebear kingdom-city in the south; in 3E 432 its Queen Clavilla attacked guild charters and called approved Satakal worship heresy.

entries.name: Elinhir
entries.summary: Crown-leaning city of Craglorn, seat of High Prophet Ayaan-si, who preaches revolt against Lhotun. Its lands were claimed by Skyrim in 3E 397.
entries.eraNote: Ayaan-si active ca. 3E 433; Skyrim claim from 3E 397.

entries.name: Dragonstar
entries.summary: Border city split into walled Redguard and Nord halves that distrust each other; violence between them is common.
entries.eraNote: Divided since the 3E 397 war; still split per 3E 432 guide.

entries.name: Hegathe
entries.summary: Southwestern port where the Yokudans first landed; the old Crown capital under the Second Empire.
entries.eraNote: City persists; Crown-capital role is Second Era.

entries.name: Gilane
entries.summary: Southwestern city in Khefrem near the ruins of Volenfell, the old Dwemer capital.
entries.eraNote: City attested across eras; 3E politics not documented.

entries.name: Skaven
entries.summary: Central Hammerfell city in Sunforge; listed among Crown places.

entries.name: Stros M'Kai
entries.summary: Southern island port where the Crowns were beaten in 2E 864 and where the treaty bringing Hammerfell into the Empire was signed.
entries.eraNote: Island and port persist; key events 2E 864.

entries.name: Bergama
entries.summary: Deep-desert barony, traditionally Crown, home of the Ra Gada Hall of Judgment; joined Sentinel after the Warp in the West.

entries.name: Satakalaam
entries.summary: Walled east Iliac Bay city where the Yokudan pantheon is still openly worshipped; part of Sentinel's realm after 3E 417.

entries.name: Totambu
entries.summary: Inland fiefdom that broke from Sentinel and sided with Ayaan-si's Crown cause, though Lhotun's lands surround it.

entries.name: Abibon-Gora
entries.summary: West-coast city and region on the Iliac Bay, absorbed into Sentinel's kingdom by the Warp in the West.

entries.name: King / Queen
entries.summary: Rulers of Redguard city-kingdoms, e.g. King Lhotun of Sentinel and Queen Clavilla of Taneth. Not for player cards without admin approval.
entries.eraNote: Named rulers in the 3E 432 Pocket Guide.

entries.name: Baron / Baroness
entries.summary: Lord of a Hammerfell barony such as Bergama or Kozanset.
entries.eraNote: Kozanset described as a Third Era barony; Bergama a barony joining Sentinel in 3E 417.

entries.name: Grandee
entries.summary: Redguard noble title borne by Yaghoub (1E Ra Gada leader) and Second Era nobles. No dedicated lore article; 3E usage unconfirmed.
entries.eraNote: Attested 1E 808 (Yaghoub) and 2E (ESO: Husni, Ebrahim). Definition rests on a UESP talk page: unverified for 3E 433.

entries.name: High Prophet
entries.summary: Religious-political leader title held by Ayaan-si of Elinhir, voice of the Crown revolt against Sentinel.

entries.name: Single given name
entries.summary: Many Redguards go by one given name (Oblivion examples: Kelvyn, Khafiz, Dahlia). Safe default for a 3E card.

entries.name: Derivation name (at-, af-, al-, do-, ibn)
entries.summary: Second name tied to a parent or place: at- direct descendant, af- other kin, al- from a place, do- birthplace, ibn son of. E.g. Arahn al-Bergama.
entries.eraNote: Examples are ESO (2E 582). No 3E counter-evidence; reviewer may allow as style.

entries.name: Yokudan pantheon
entries.summary: The old Redguard gods (Satakal, Ruptga, Tu'whacca, Morwha, Zeht, Tava, Onsi, Leki and others). Core faith of the Crowns and desert tribes.
entries.eraNote: Still worshipped in 3E (Satakalaam; Crown faith per 3E 432 guide).

entries.name: Divines (Forebear practice)
entries.summary: Forebears largely follow the Imperial Divines, sometimes under Yokudan names (Tu'whacca for Arkay, Zeht for Zenithar). Crowns see this as betrayal.

entries.name: Ancestor reverence
entries.summary: Redguards honor their dead intensely; corpses are sacred, mummification is practiced and disturbing a tomb is sacrilege.

entries.name: Satakal
entries.summary: The serpent Worldskin, god of everything, endlessly shedding and devouring itself. Revered by Crowns and Alik'r nomads.
entries.eraNote: Worship active in 3E 432 (called heresy by Queen Clavilla).

entries.name: Ruptga (Tall Papa)
entries.summary: Chief of the Yokudan gods, lord of the stars and of the Far Shores afterlife.

entries.name: Tu'whacca
entries.summary: Clever shepherd of souls who guides Redguards to the Far Shores. Forebear regions often treat him as Arkay.

entries.name: Morwha
entries.summary: Yokudan goddess of fertility and love, Tall Papa's favored wife; sometimes conflated with Mara.

entries.name: Zeht
entries.summary: Yokudan god of farming, food, law and mathematics; Forebears may worship him as Zenithar.

entries.name: Tava
entries.summary: Bird goddess of air and weather, patron of sailors; her myths were absorbed into Kynareth's.

entries.name: Onsi (Boneshaver)
entries.summary: Warrior god of the Ra Gada and patron of swordcraft; the Boneshaver saber is his legendary gift.

entries.name: Leki
entries.summary: Saint of the Spirit Sword, goddess of unorthodox swordsmanship; desert schools at Leki's Blade train in her name.

entries.name: HoonDing (Make Way God)
entries.summary: Spirit of perseverance that appears when the Redguards must clear a path for their people. Not the same as Talos.
entries.eraNote: Now a faded local spirit of the Dragontails.

entries.name: Cyrodiil
entries.summary: The Imperial Province at the heart of Tamriel, split culturally into Colovia (west) and Nibenay (east) around the Imperial City.

entries.name: Colovian
entries.summary: Western Imperials: frontier folk with strong Nordic roots, plain or martial in dress, devout to the Divines, and the backbone of the Legion.

entries.name: Nibenese
entries.summary: Eastern Imperials of the Niben valley: showy dress, tattoos and brands, cults and ceremony, a battlemage aristocracy. Seen as the high culture of Cyrodiil.

entries.name: Heartlander
entries.summary: Nibenese subculture around the Imperial City; secular-leaning, treating faith as a private matter.

entries.name: Nibenese tattoos
entries.summary: Tattoos and brandings that mark a Nibenese person's faith, political faction or way of life.
entries.eraNote: Cultural practice; also Oblivion-era face tattoos on Imperial NPCs.

entries.name: Nedic ancestry
entries.summary: Pre-Imperial human peoples of Tamriel. The Nibenese are described as the closest living thing to pure Nedes.
entries.eraNote: Merethic and early First Era peoples.

entries.name: Kothringi (not Imperial)
entries.summary: Silver-skinned human tribe of Black Marsh, probably Nedic, wiped out by the Knahaten Flu. Not Imperials; ancestry only, with an explicit lore caveat.

entries.name: Colovia (Colovian West)
entries.summary: Western Cyrodiil: Gold Coast, West Weald, Colovian Highlands, Great Forest. Core counties Anvil, Chorrol, Kvatch, Skingrad.
entries.eraNote: Geography and counties as in Oblivion.

entries.name: Nibenay (Nibenean East)
entries.summary: Eastern Cyrodiil along the Niben: counties Bravil, Bruma, Cheydinhal, Leyawiin, plus the Heartlands around City Isle.

entries.name: Heartlands
entries.summary: Central lands around Lake Rumare and the Imperial City.

entries.name: Imperial City
entries.summary: Capital of the Empire on City Isle; Nibenese in style, with Ayleid walls and White-Gold Tower. Seat of the Elder Council.

entries.name: Anvil
entries.summary: Colovian port county on the Gold Coast.

entries.name: Kvatch
entries.summary: Hilltop Colovian county on the Gold Coast, sacked by Daedra early in the Oblivion Crisis. Strong hook for refugee characters.

entries.name: Skingrad
entries.summary: Colovian county in the West Weald, known for wine.

entries.name: Chorrol
entries.summary: Main town of the Colovian Highlands.

entries.name: Bruma
entries.summary: Jerall Mountains county, Nibenese in custom but mostly Nord in people and building. Holds the Great Chapel of Talos; besieged by Daedra in 3E 433.

entries.name: Cheydinhal
entries.summary: Nibenese county by the Valus Mountains with Dunmeri touches in its architecture.

entries.name: Bravil
entries.summary: Nibenese county on Niben Bay in the Nibenay Valley.
entries.eraNote: County in 3E 433; seceded briefly in early 4E.

entries.name: Leyawiin
entries.summary: Southern Nibenese county, roughly the same as the Blackwood region.
entries.eraNote: County in 3E 433; seceded briefly in early 4E.

entries.name: Septim Dynasty
entries.summary: Ruling imperial line. Uriel VII and his known heirs are murdered in 3E 433; Martin dies ending the Crisis. Claiming Septim blood should be admin-only.
entries.eraNote: Reigning at the start of 3E 433; line ends with Martin at the end of the Crisis.

entries.name: Mede Dynasty
entries.summary: Colovian dynasty founded when Titus Mede takes the Imperial City. Does not exist yet in 3E 433.

entries.name: Elder Council
entries.summary: Cyrodiil's governing council in the Imperial Palace; handles taxes and laws and rules between emperors. Led by High Chancellor Ocato in 3E 433.

entries.name: Imperial Legion
entries.summary: The Empire's army; garrisons forts and lends guards to cities and nobles. Colovians fill most ranks. Open to any race.

entries.name: Imperial Watch
entries.summary: Name used for the guards protecting the Emperor and the Imperial Province; the Imperial City's guard in Oblivion.

entries.name: Blades
entries.summary: Akaviri-rooted bodyguards and spies of the Emperor. Members renounce former titles; led by Grandmaster Jauffre at Cloud Ruler Temple in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Active 3E 433; outlawed by the White-Gold Concordat 4E 175.

entries.name: Imperial Battlemages
entries.summary: War-mages rooted in the old Nibenese ruling class; still an aristocratic tradition in the Niben.

entries.name: Colovian Estates
entries.summary: Autonomous league of western merchant-estates, traditionally Anvil, Chorrol, Kvatch and Skingrad. Good ancestry flavor for old Colovian families.
entries.eraNote: Prominent in 1E-2E; 3E 433 standing not documented. Unverified.

entries.name: Penitus Oculatus
entries.summary: Imperial security and intelligence service that replaces the Blades after the Septims fall. Not available in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Fourth Era; earliest dated mention ca. 4E 40.

entries.name: Emperor
entries.summary: Ruler of Tamriel from the Ruby Throne; Uriel Septim VII until his murder in 3E 433. Not a player title.

entries.name: High Chancellor
entries.summary: Head of the Elder Council and its Inner Council; often also the Imperial Battlemage.

entries.name: Count / Countess
entries.summary: Ruler of a Cyrodiil county such as Anvil or Skingrad (e.g. Count Marius Caro). Lesser nobles may use Lord or Lady.

entries.name: Potentate
entries.summary: Steward ruling in all but name when no heir exists; held by the Akaviri in 2E and taken by Ocato only after the Crisis.
entries.eraNote: 2E Akaviri Potentates; Ocato's tenure ends 4E 15. Not current during 3E 433 gameplay.

entries.name: Nine Divines
entries.summary: Akatosh, Arkay, Dibella, Julianos, Kynareth, Mara, Stendarr, Zenithar and Talos. State faith of the Empire; Talos worship is lawful in 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Talos banned only after the White-Gold Concordat (4E 175).

entries.name: Nibenese cults
entries.summary: Eastern devotions alongside the Divines: Ancestor-Moth, hero cults of Reman and Tiber Septim, animal and ancestor spirits.

entries.name: Shor (Colovian Shezarr)
entries.summary: Colovians honor Shezarr under the Nordic name Shor, a mark of their northern roots.

entries.name: Latinate given name + family name
entries.summary: Roman-style names, men often -us, women often -ia (Marius Caro, Arriana Valga). Family names recur across games.

entries.name: Epithet
entries.summary: Commoners and rogues often carry a nickname instead of or after a surname: 'X the Y' or an adjective first (Imus the Dull, Luckless Lucina).

entries.name: High Rock
entries.summary: Northwestern province of feuding Breton kingdoms; after the Warp in the West it has about five kingdoms instead of about a hundred.

entries.name: Systres Archipelago
entries.summary: Abecean Sea islands (High Isle, Galen, Amenos, Y'ffelon) settled by Breton workers and older druid circles; still mostly Breton in culture by 3E 433.
entries.eraNote: Culture largely Breton by 3E 433; 3E government unclear (some ca. 3E 427 maps show it as Hammerfell).

entries.name: Direnni descent
entries.summary: Claimed elven blood from Clan Direnni, the Altmer who mixed with the Nedes and later ruled High Rock. Many Breton nobles play this down.

entries.name: Manmer (proto-Breton)
entries.summary: Early half-elven ancestors of the Bretons, more elf-like in look. Ancestry note only; a living Manmer in 3E 433 is not supported.

entries.name: Druids of Galen (Nedic side)
entries.summary: The Nedic people of the Systres remembered as the human ancestors of the Bretons.

entries.name: Reachfolk (Reachmen)
entries.summary: A distinct human people of the Reach, mixed from many stocks and distantly related to Bretons, who do not count them as kin. Rendered with the Breton body.
entries.eraNote: Attested 1E through 4E; no specific 3E 433 record on the pages read.

entries.name: Forsworn
entries.summary: Name for Reach rebels after Markarth was retaken from Madanach's uprising. Not usable in 3E 433.

entries.name: Glenmoril Wyrd
entries.summary: Women-only Breton nature-witch covens, mostly devoted to Hircine. Open to any race. No coven left in Cyrodiil by 3E 433; covens remain in High Rock and Skyrim.
entries.eraNote: Covens active 3E 427 (Solstheim); none in Cyrodiil by 3E 433.

entries.name: Druids (Y'ffre's True Way)
entries.summary: Nature-steward faith of the old Bretons, from which the Wyrd split. Ancestry or flavor only.

entries.name: Knights of the Dragon
entries.summary: Knightly order of the Kingdom of Daggerfall. Knights are styled Sir or Dame.
entries.eraNote: Latest dated record 3E 405; said to continue to modern times. 3E 433 not explicitly confirmed.

entries.name: Knights of the Rose
entries.summary: Knightly order tied to Wayrest.

entries.name: Knights of the Flame
entries.summary: Knightly order tied to Anticlere.

entries.name: Glenumbra
entries.summary: Western High Rock peninsula holding Daggerfall and Camlorn.
entries.eraNote: Geography; region name mostly from ESO-era sources.

entries.name: Stormhaven
entries.summary: Eastern Iliac Bay region around Wayrest and Alcaire.
entries.eraNote: Geography; region name mostly from ESO-era sources.

entries.name: Rivenspire
entries.summary: Northern highlands holding Shornhelm and Northpoint.
entries.eraNote: Geography; region name mostly from ESO-era sources.

entries.name: Bangkorai
entries.summary: Border region with Hammerfell; its northern part holds Evermore.

entries.name: Daggerfall
entries.summary: Western kingdom covering much of High Rock after 3E 417. Its prince Camaron, son of Gothryd and the Redguard Aubk-i, wed Camlorn's heiress.

entries.name: Wayrest
entries.summary: Eastern Iliac Bay kingdom under Queen Elysana, feared and newly allied with Orsinium.

entries.name: Camlorn
entries.summary: Northwestern realm of Duke Senhyn, bound to Daggerfall by marriage and quarrelling with Northpoint and Evermore over borders.

entries.name: Northpoint
entries.summary: Northern kingdom that grew by swallowing neighbors after 3E 417; insular and wary.

entries.name: Evermore
entries.summary: Inland kingdom that expanded after 3E 417 and keeps to itself. Founded 1E 983.

entries.name: Shornhelm
entries.summary: Old Rivenspire capital. Its 3E 433 status is not stated in the 3E 432 guide.
entries.eraNote: City exists; political status in 3E 433 unverified.

entries.name: Farrun
entries.summary: Eastern High Rock city near Wrothgar. 3E 433 status not stated.
entries.eraNote: City exists; political status in 3E 433 unverified.

entries.name: Jehanna
entries.summary: Eastern High Rock city; UESP's Forebears page lists it among lands Skyrim seized in 3E 397.
entries.eraNote: Possibly under Skyrim's claim since 3E 397; needs verification.

entries.name: Balfiera (Direnni Tower)
entries.summary: Iliac Bay isle of the Adamantine Tower, old Direnni seat and neutral meeting ground; fell under one of the four Bay powers after 3E 417.

entries.name: Royal house of Daggerfall
entries.summary: Line of King Gothryd and Queen Aubk-i, whose marriage sealed peace with Sentinel; Prince Camaron is half Redguard.

entries.name: Clan Direnni
entries.summary: Altmer merchant clan that ruled High Rock in the early First Era and fathered the Breton line. Not Breton itself; usable only as ancestry.
entries.eraNote: Hegemony ended ca. 1E 498; 3E 433 existence not stated.

entries.name: Old noble houses (Dufort, Montclair, Tamrith, Guimard, Mornard, Cumberland)
entries.summary: Breton houses known mainly from the Second Era. Fine as family ancestry; their 3E standing is not documented.

entries.name: King / Queen
entries.summary: Rulers of the Breton kingdoms; their children are Princes and Princesses. Addressed as Your Majesty.
entries.eraNote: Elysana of Wayrest, Gothryd of Daggerfall in 3E 432.

entries.name: Duke / Duchess
entries.summary: High noble ruler, addressed as Your Grace; e.g. Duke Senhyn of Camlorn.

entries.name: Marquis, Count, Viscount, Baron, Lord, Earl
entries.summary: Lesser Breton ranks; barons often hold the title without land. Earls also appear (Jakben, Earl of Imbel).
entries.eraNote: General Breton usage; Earl attested in Morrowind (3E 427).

entries.name: Sir / Dame
entries.summary: Address for knights of a Breton order. Orders once took only the high-born, later merchants too.

entries.name: Eight and Nine Divines
entries.summary: Most Bretons took up the Divines under the Alessian Empire; Daedra worship is generally frowned on.

entries.name: Phynaster
entries.summary: Patron 'teacher' god of the Direnni, still honored by some Bretons proud of elven descent.
entries.eraNote: Listed in the Breton pantheon; minor cult.

entries.name: French-style given name + surname
entries.summary: Bretons use first name plus family name, often French-sounding (Gaston Surilie, Eduard Denile). Nobles may add 'of' plus a holding.

entries.name: Skyrim
entries.summary: Cold northern Nord province, a kingdom under a High King with jarls ruling holds. In 3E 432 its cities feud and expand while border war with Hammerfell simmers.

entries.name: Western Skyrim
entries.summary: Rugged west of Skyrim with harsh ground and dangerous beasts. Covers holds such as Haafingar, Hjaalmarch, the Reach and Falkreath (grouping is our reading).
entries.eraNote: Remastered Origin; hold grouping not defined by UESP, inferred from geography.

entries.name: Eastern Skyrim (Old Holds)
entries.summary: Storm-beaten east of Skyrim; the Old Holds of Winterhold, Eastmarch, the Rift and the Pale. Origin text nods to the College of Winterhold.
entries.eraNote: Remastered Origin; Old Holds grouping from Lore:Nord.

entries.name: Atmoran descent
entries.summary: Nords trace their blood to Atmora, the frozen northern continent they left in waves; Ysgramor is the model ancestor.

entries.name: Descent from Ysgramor's Five Hundred
entries.summary: Family claim to one of the Five Hundred Companions who came with Ysgramor. A boast, not provable.

entries.name: Skaal
entries.summary: Nord offshoot tribe of northeast Solstheim; hospitable, nature-revering, worshipping the All-Maker instead of the Nordic gods.

entries.name: Bruma Nords (Cyrodiil)
entries.summary: Nord majority of Bruma in the Jerall Mountains; Nordic in building and faith but living under Nibenese law and custom.

entries.name: Haafingar
entries.summary: Northwestern hold of Solitude, which in 3E 432 is gaining power through marriage alliances and annexations.
entries.eraNote: Hold system attested 2E and 4E; Solitude's rise in 3E 432 guide.

entries.name: Eastmarch
entries.summary: Eastern hold of Windhelm, one of the Old Holds.
entries.eraNote: Hold system attested 2E and 4E; 3E 433 jarls not documented.

entries.name: Whiterun
entries.summary: Central hold; in 3E 432 a self-styled Lorkhan priestess, the Witch-Queen Jsashe, holds the city after years of feuds and hardship.

entries.name: The Rift
entries.summary: Southeastern hold of Riften, one of the Old Holds.
entries.eraNote: Hold system attested 2E and 4E; 3E 433 jarls not documented.

entries.name: The Pale
entries.summary: Northern hold of Dawnstar, allied by marriage with Solitude in 3E 432.

entries.name: Winterhold
entries.summary: Northeastern hold whose city revived in 3E 432 as refugees and scholars gathered at its College.

entries.name: Hjaalmarch
entries.summary: Marshy northern hold with its seat at Morthal.
entries.eraNote: Hold system attested 2E and 4E; 3E 433 jarls not documented.

entries.name: Falkreath
entries.summary: Southern forested hold bordering Cyrodiil, seat at Falkreath.
entries.eraNote: Hold system attested 2E and 4E; 3E 433 jarls not documented.

entries.name: The Reach
entries.summary: Southwestern hold of Markarth with only a thin Nord majority; homeland of the Reachfolk.

entries.name: Solstheim
entries.summary: Island north of Morrowind, home of the Skaal. By 3E 433 Skyrim's Nords are campaigning to take it over; the Legion still holds Fort Frostmoth.
entries.eraNote: Skyrim campaign starts 3E 433; ceded to Morrowind 4E 16.

entries.name: Companions
entries.summary: Honor-bound mercenaries of Jorrvaskr in Whiterun who claim the legacy of Ysgramor's Five Hundred. Their werewolf secret is lore, not a card option.
entries.eraNote: Harbinger list implies continuity through 3E; no 3E 433 record. Best attested 4E 201.

entries.name: Greybeards
entries.summary: Hermit masters of the Thu'um at High Hrothgar. Lore background only; not a joinable faction or playable power.

entries.name: College of Winterhold
entries.summary: Mage school drawing scholars back to Winterhold in 3E 432. Open to any race.

entries.name: Hörme
entries.summary: Outlaw movement still raiding Imperial targets in 3E 432, holding that Potema's line were the true Septims. An outlaw or villain option.

entries.name: Stormcloaks
entries.summary: Ulfric Stormcloak's rebellion against the Empire. Does not exist in 3E 433.

entries.name: High King / High Queen
entries.summary: Ruler of all Skyrim, chosen by the jarls at the Moot. Not a player title.

entries.name: Jarl
entries.summary: Ruler of a hold. Named jarls for 3E 433 are not documented, so cards should not claim a specific seat.
entries.eraNote: Title attested across eras; 3E 433 holders unknown.

entries.name: Tongue (Thu'um user)
entries.summary: Nord who can Shout, seen as Kyne's gift. Lore only; not a card option in OB:MP.

entries.name: Nordic pantheon
entries.summary: Old Nord gods led by Kyne, with Shor, Tsun, Stuhn, Mara, Dibella, Jhunal and Ysmir (Talos). Worshipped beside the Divines, including in Bruma.

entries.name: All-Maker (Skaal faith)
entries.summary: Skaal belief in a kind but unknowable creator and nature spirits, opposed by the Adversary in forms such as the Greedy Man.

entries.name: Kyne
entries.summary: Head of the Nord gods, a fiercer, warrior form of Kynareth; source of the Thu'um.

entries.name: Shor
entries.summary: Dead god who rules Sovngarde, the hall of worthy Nord dead.

entries.name: Tsun
entries.summary: God of trials in the face of hardship.

entries.name: Stuhn
entries.summary: God of ransom, brotherhood and justice.

entries.name: Mara
entries.summary: Mother goddess, in Nord myth the handmaiden of Kyne.

entries.name: Dibella
entries.summary: Goddess of beauty and the muse of artists.

entries.name: Jhunal
entries.summary: God of runes and of hermetic orders.

entries.name: Ysmir (Talos)
entries.summary: The Nord name for Talos, the deified Tiber Septim, 'Dragon of the North'. Lawful worship in 3E 433.

entries.name: Orkey (Testing God)
entries.summary: One of the Testing Gods with Herma-Mora and Mauloch. Nords guard against them; they are not worshipped. Do not offer as a patron.

entries.name: Given name + hyphenated epithet
entries.summary: Short Germanic name plus a descriptive byname (Hans Black-Nail, Heinrich Oaken-Hull) or 'the' title (Algot the Northerner).

entries.name: Patronymic surname (-sen / -son, -dottir)
entries.summary: Surname from a parent's name: -sen or -son for 'son of', -dottir for 'daughter of' (Eriksen, Engelsdottir). The phrase 'X, son of Y' is not documented.
entries.eraNote: Arena and Daggerfall (late 3E), books, ESO, Skyrim.

entries.name: Skyrim-era clan names (Battle-Born, Gray-Mane, Black-Briar)
entries.summary: Specific Whiterun and Riften families from 4E 201. The compound style is fine, but these exact families should not be claimed.

entries.name: Maternal race rule
entries.summary: Children of mixed men and mer usually take the mother's race, sometimes with traces of the father. Not absolute: siblings can differ.
entries.eraNote: Notes on Racial Phylogeny, a book found in Oblivion.

entries.name: Cyro-Nord (Imperial-Nord)
entries.summary: Mixed Imperial and Nord descent. Colovians themselves descend from Cyro-Nord settlers; Uriel VII had a Nord ancestor.

entries.name: Breton-Redguard
entries.summary: Attested mix; Prince Camaron of Daggerfall is the son of a Breton king and a Redguard queen.

entries.name: Breton-Imperial
entries.summary: Attested mix with examples in Oblivion (Matthias Draconis, Ida Ottus).

entries.name: Imperial-Redguard
entries.summary: Attested mix; one known example has lighter skin than most Redguards.
entries.eraNote: ESO example; pairing valid in any era.

entries.name: Breton-Nord
entries.summary: Attested mix; children of one couple can split, some Nord and some Breton.
entries.eraNote: Examples from Skyrim and older lore; pairing valid in any era.

entries.name: Nord-Redguard
entries.summary: Listed as an attested human pairing on UESP's multiraciality page.

entries.name: Human-mer (half-elf)
entries.summary: Men and mer have fertile children. Card race follows the mother; Bretons are the classic old case, and Oblivion has several half-mer NPCs.
entries.eraNote: Notes on Racial Phylogeny; Oblivion examples.

entries.name: Orc-human
entries.summary: The Healers' book calls Orc fertility with others unproven, yet Oblivion's Gray Prince has an Orc mother and Imperial father. Allow with a caution.

entries.name: Beastfolk crosses (Khajiit, Argonian)
entries.summary: Whether beast races can breed with men or mer is unclear in lore; reports exist but none are confirmed. Block on cards by default.

entries.name: Half-Giant
entries.summary: Rare documented human-giant offspring. Cannot be represented by any Oblivion body model.

entries.name: Temple ward
entries.summary: Left at or taken in by a chapel of the Nine and brought up by its priests. Knows the liturgy, the healing rites and the charity rolls better than any family home.

entries.name: Street orphan
entries.summary: Grew up without parents in a city slum, begging, running errands and learning to steal. In Cyrodiil such children often fall in with the beggars who quietly serve the Thieves Guild.

entries.name: Noble household
entries.summary: Raised in a count's or lord's household with tutors, servants and court manners, but never quite in line for the title. Expected to marry well or serve the family name.

entries.name: Farmstead
entries.summary: Raised on a farm far from the walls, up before dawn for planting, herding and harvest. Knows weather, soil and livestock, and how thin a farm's margin is in a bad year.

entries.name: Caravan life
entries.summary: Grew up on the road with a trading caravan, moving goods between cities. Learned to haggle, mend wagons, read the road for bandits and sleep anywhere.

entries.name: Legion family
entries.summary: Child of a soldier, raised around garrison forts and drill yards. Moved with each posting and learned discipline, rank and the Legion's ways before learning a trade.

entries.name: Sailor's family
entries.summary: Raised in a port by a family that worked the ships, often waiting months for a parent to return. Knows knots, tides and the gossip of harbours from Anvil to the Iliac Bay.

entries.name: Raised abroad
entries.summary: Brought up in a province far from the family's homeland, among another people. Speaks with their accent and keeps their customs, and is seen as a foreigner by both sides.

entries.name: Mixed household
entries.summary: Child of parents from two different races. Lore holds that a child usually takes the mother's race, perhaps with a trace of the father, and grows up between two sets of customs.

entries.name: Innkeeper's child
entries.summary: Grew up behind the counter of a roadside inn or city tavern, serving travellers and hearing every rumour. Knows people, drink and when a brawl is about to start.

entries.name: Mining camp
entries.summary: Raised in a camp beside an iron or ore mine, where the work is dark, dangerous and badly paid. Grew up strong, wary of cave-ins and of whatever lives deeper in the tunnels.

entries.name: Raised in the wilds
entries.summary: Raised by a hunter or hermit in a remote cabin, far from towns and law. Learned to track, snare and forage, but finds crowds and city rules strange.

entries.name: War refugee
entries.summary: Family fled a war zone during the child's early years, such as the Arnesian War or the strife around the Iliac Bay before the Warp in the West. Grew up poor in a new land, starting over.
entries.eraNote: Arnesian War c. 3E 396; Warp in the West 3E 417. Both fit a character aged about 16 to 40 in 3E 433.

entries.name: Old Summerset bloodline
entries.summary: Born into an old Summerset family that tracks its ancestry back to the Aldmer. Every step, from schooling to marriage, followed set forms and the family's standing.

entries.name: Scholar's household
entries.summary: Raised among archivists and mages in one of Summerset's learned cities. Childhood was lessons, copying texts and formal debate, with little room for play.

entries.name: Auridon port family
entries.summary: Grew up in a harbour town on Auridon, where Imperial ships and foreign traders call. More used to outsiders than most High Elves, and looked down on a little for it.

entries.name: Imperial-born High Elf
entries.summary: Born to Altmer settled in Cyrodiil, for example in the Imperial City's Elven Gardens. Knows Summerset mostly from family stories and speaks Cyrodilic first.

entries.name: Hatched under the Hist
entries.summary: Hatched among the roots of a village Hist tree in Black Marsh and raised by the whole clutch-community. Took the sap at the naming rite and still feels the Hist's pull.

entries.name: Slave in Morrowind
entries.summary: Captured or sold as a child and raised as a slave on a Dunmer plantation or in a House household. Slavery is still lawful in Morrowind in 3E 433, so escape means a life on the run.
entries.eraNote: Current: the Armistice lets Morrowind keep slavery in 3E 433; elsewhere in the Empire it is banned.

entries.name: Freed or escaped slave
entries.summary: Born or sold into slavery in Morrowind, then freed by an owner or smuggled out by abolitionists like the Twin Lamps. Carries old scars and a deep distrust of Dunmer masters.

entries.name: Hatched outside Black Marsh
entries.summary: Hatched and raised far from the Hist, for example in Leyawiin or Bravil. Lore says such Argonians cannot hear the Hist, and kin from the marsh may treat them as half-lost.

entries.name: Imperial port city
entries.summary: Raised in a coastal city like Gideon or Lilmoth, where Imperial traders, soldiers and Archein elites rule. Learned Cyrodilic and the ways of outsiders alongside marsh custom.

entries.name: Tree-city born
entries.summary: Grew up high in the boughs of a graht-oak city such as Elden Root. Bound by the Green Pact from birth: eats meat, never harms the forest's plants.

entries.name: Wandering hunting clan
entries.summary: Raised in a small clan that roams the deep forest, living by the hunt and the Green Pact. Knows bow, trail and old stories better than towns or coin.

entries.name: Coastal trading town
entries.summary: Raised in a Valenwood port like Woodhearth or Haven, where foreign ships trade. Learned to deal with outsiders, and that not everyone shares Bosmer views on meat and wood.

entries.name: Raised in Cyrodiil
entries.summary: Born to Bosmer living in an Imperial town. Grew up outside the Green Pact's reach, used to wooden furniture and bread, which elders back home find shocking.

entries.name: Noble court
entries.summary: Raised at the court of a Breton kingdom such as Daggerfall or Wayrest, amid intrigue, chivalry and arranged marriages. Learned etiquette, swordplay and a little magic.

entries.name: Village under a manor
entries.summary: Grew up in a peasant village beholden to a local lord, working fields and paying dues. High Rock's countless petty lords make for a hard and quarrelsome countryside.

entries.name: Iliac Bay port
entries.summary: Raised in a busy Iliac Bay harbour town among merchants, sailors and smugglers of many races. Used to foreign coin, foreign tongues and politics that change with the tide.

entries.name: Family of spellcasters
entries.summary: Raised in a household where magic was everyday, as is common among Bretons. Cast small spells before learning letters and was expected to join the Mages Guild.

entries.name: Reach clan
entries.summary: Raised among the Reachfolk of the western mountains, a hardy mixed people with their own clans and old gods. Neither Nord nor High Rock Breton fully trusts them.
entries.eraNote: Reachmen are a distinct Breton-related people; in 3E 433 the Reach is part of Skyrim.

entries.name: House Hlaalu family
entries.summary: Raised in a Hlaalu household, where trade, deals and friendly ties with the Empire are the family business. Learned to bargain and to smile at outlanders.

entries.name: House Redoran family
entries.summary: Raised in a stern Redoran household that values duty, honour and the Temple. Taught to fight, to obey the councils and to keep a straight face in hard times.

entries.name: Telvanni household
entries.summary: Grew up in the service of a Telvanni wizard in a grown mushroom tower. Learned that power, magical power above all, sets your worth, and that rules are for the weak.

entries.name: Ashlander tribe
entries.summary: Raised among nomadic Ashlanders, living in yurts and following herds across the wastes. Honours ancestors and the wise women, and distrusts the Great Houses and the Empire.

entries.name: Emigrant to Cyrodiil
entries.summary: Raised in a Dunmer family that left Morrowind for Cyrodiil, likely Cheydinhal, where the Count himself is Dunmer. Keeps the old customs but grew up in Imperial streets.

entries.name: Colovian family
entries.summary: Raised in the hilly west of Cyrodiil in a plain, hard-working, devout household. Colovians prize martial skill, frugality and old tradition, and many sons and daughters join the Legion.

entries.name: Nibenese family
entries.summary: Raised in the eastern Niben valley, where people love bright clothes, tattoos, ceremony and philosophy. Grew up amid temple rites, bureaucracy and endless talk.

entries.name: Imperial City born
entries.summary: Born within the White-Gold walls and raised among its districts, markets and the Arena's roar. Proud of the capital and a little dismissive of the provinces.

entries.name: Gold Coast trading family
entries.summary: Raised in Anvil or Kvatch among merchants, sailors and vintners of the western coast. Grew up with the sea trade, foreign ships and Colovian pride.

entries.name: Trading caravan
entries.summary: Born to a wandering Khajiit caravan that trades across Tamriel. Grew up with tents, campfires, haggling and moon sugar tales, and is often watched closely by city guards.

entries.name: Southern estate family
entries.summary: Raised in the jungles and river basins of southern Elsweyr, on a family estate growing saltrice or moon sugar. Learned refined manners, old trade customs and estate life.

entries.name: Northern nomad pride
entries.summary: Raised in a nomadic pride on the dry northern plains of Elsweyr, where clans raid, herd and wander. Learned to fight, ride the dunes and follow a strong chief.

entries.name: Raised by the Moon priests
entries.summary: Raised in a temple of the Riddle'Thar and the moon faith, steeped in the Two-Moons Dance and the Mane's teachings. Learned riddles, rites and the Khajiit view of the gods.

entries.name: Border-town raised
entries.summary: Raised in a Cyrodiil town near Elsweyr, such as Leyawiin or Bravil, among Imperials who often distrust Khajiit. Learned Imperial ways and quick wits to survive suspicion.

entries.name: Raised in a Hold city
entries.summary: Grew up in the city seat of one of Skyrim's holds, under the eye of its jarl and in the shadow of the mead hall. Knows clan feuds, songs of old heroes and hard winters.

entries.name: Northern coast village
entries.summary: Raised in a fishing or whaling village on the icy Sea of Ghosts. Grew up hauling nets, braving storms and fearing what rises from the cold water.

entries.name: Skaal village
entries.summary: Raised among the Skaal of Solstheim, Nords who hold to the All-Maker and a simple life of hunting and fishing. Wary of the Empire and of outsiders' greed.

entries.name: Nord of Bruma
entries.summary: Born to Nord settlers in Bruma, high in the Jerall Mountains of Cyrodiil. Keeps Nord customs and mead halls, but grew up as an Imperial subject.

entries.name: Stronghold-born
entries.summary: Born in a walled Orc stronghold ruled by a chief under the Code of Malacath. Grew up with blacksmith fires, hard labour and the rule that strength settles disputes.

entries.name: Child of new Orsinium
entries.summary: Raised in the Orc kingdom Gortwog refounded in 3E 399, amid the hope of finally being recognised as a province. Proud of Orc statehood and wary of Breton neighbours.
entries.eraNote: Orsinium refounded 3E 399; provincial status still pending in 3E 433.

entries.name: Raised in a human city
entries.summary: Grew up outside the strongholds, in a city of Men, perhaps as a smith's or soldier's child. Orcs are prized in the Legion and as armorers, but still meet open prejudice.

entries.name: Family cast out
entries.summary: Raised by parents exiled from their stronghold for breaking the Code of Malacath. Lived on the edges, between Orc tradition and towns that did not want them either.

entries.name: Crowns family
entries.summary: Raised in a traditional Crowns household that honours Yokudan custom, the old nobility and ancestor ways. Taught that Hammerfell's true heirs are the old Yokudan line.

entries.name: Forebears family
entries.summary: Raised in a Forebear trading family in a port like Sentinel or Taneth. Forebears are open to foreigners and to the Empire, and value trade, travel and new ideas.

entries.name: Alik'r desert nomads
entries.summary: Raised among desert tribes of the Alik'r, moving between oases and trading posts. Learned to read the sands, find water and fight off raiders.

entries.name: Raised at a sword school
entries.summary: Brought up in a fighting school that keeps the Redguard warrior tradition. Days of drills, discipline and respect for the blade, with tales of the sword-singers of old.
entries.eraNote: The sword-singers (Ansei) are largely a historical tradition; the school itself is a generic Redguard martial upbringing.

entries.name: High nobility
entries.summary: Born to a ruling house: a count's, king's or jarl's family. Holds land, rank and privilege, plus the duties and feuds that come with them.

entries.name: Minor nobility
entries.summary: Of a lesser noble or knightly family: a title and a coat of arms, but little land or money. Serves a greater lord to keep the family name up.

entries.name: Landed gentry
entries.summary: Owns an estate, vineyard or farmland worked by tenants, without a noble title. Comfortable, respected locally and keen to marry into nobility.

entries.name: Wealthy merchant
entries.summary: From a rich trading family whose wealth rivals the nobility. Has coin, contacts and ships or shops, but no birthright to rule.

entries.name: Guild artisan
entries.summary: A skilled crafter or guild member with a recognised trade and a place in town life. Owns tools, maybe a shop, and earns an honest living.

entries.name: Free commoner
entries.summary: An ordinary free subject of the Empire: labourer, shop clerk or townsfolk. No title, no master, and no safety net beyond family and friends.

entries.name: Peasant
entries.summary: Works someone else's land as a tenant farmer and owes rent, crops or labour to a lord. Common in High Rock and Skyrim, and in the Cyrodiil countryside.

entries.name: Servant
entries.summary: Works in someone's household as a maid, cook, valet or groom. Free and paid, but has little time or standing of their own.

entries.name: Bonded labourer
entries.summary: Bound by contract or debt to work for a master for a set time. Legally free, unlike a slave, but cannot leave until the debt is paid.
entries.eraNote: Debt bondage is not described in detail in lore; treat it as contract-bound labour, distinct from slavery.

entries.name: Slave
entries.summary: Owned as property by a master. In 3E 433 only Morrowind still allows slavery; Argonians and Khajiit are the most common slaves there.
entries.eraNote: Current, but only lawful in Morrowind under the Armistice; illegal elsewhere in the Empire. Abolished in Morrowind in the early Fourth Era.

entries.name: Freed slave
entries.summary: Once a slave in Morrowind, now free by purchase, release or escape. Free in law outside Morrowind, but marked by the past and wary of slavers.
entries.eraNote: Current in 3E 433; escaped slaves inside Morrowind can still be reclaimed.

entries.name: Outcast or exile
entries.summary: Cast out by family, clan, house or homeland, for a crime, a feud or a forbidden belief. Belongs nowhere, owes no one and is trusted by few.

entries.name: Clergy
entries.summary: Ordained or vowed member of a temple or faith, such as the Nine Divines or the Tribunal Temple. Respected and protected, but bound by vows and duty.

entries.name: Tribal clan member
entries.summary: Belongs to a clan that lives outside Imperial class lines, like the Ashlanders, the Reachfolk or the Skaal. Rank comes from the clan, not from Imperial law.

entries.name: Farmer
entries.summary: Grew grain, vegetables or fruit and kept a few animals. Used to long days, hard labour and worrying about weather and raiders.

entries.name: Fisher
entries.summary: Fished rivers, lakes or coastal waters for a living and sold the catch at market. Knows boats, nets and the moods of the water.

entries.name: Hunter
entries.summary: Hunted deer, boar and other game for meat and hides. Good with a bow, patient and at home in the wilds.

entries.name: Trapper
entries.summary: Set snares and traps for fur-bearing animals and sold the pelts. Spent long seasons alone in forests and mountains.

entries.name: Miner
entries.summary: Dug iron, silver or other ore out of the earth in cramped, dangerous tunnels. Strong, used to dark and to the risk of collapse.

entries.name: Blacksmith
entries.summary: Worked a forge making tools, horseshoes and nails, and repairing anything iron. Strong arms, burned hands and an eye for good metal.

entries.name: Armorer
entries.summary: Made and repaired armour and weapons for guards, soldiers and adventurers. Knows steel, leather and how a blade or a plate fails.

entries.name: Tailor
entries.summary: Cut and sewed clothing for townsfolk or nobles. Knows fabric, fashion and the gossip of every customer who came for a fitting.

entries.name: Cook
entries.summary: Cooked for a tavern, a noble kitchen or a garrison. Knows food, spices and how to feed many people on little coin.

entries.name: Innkeeper
entries.summary: Ran or worked in an inn, serving drink, renting rooms and keeping the peace. Hears every rumour that passes along the road.

entries.name: Sailor
entries.summary: Crewed merchant ships or naval vessels along Tamriel's coasts. Knows rigging, ports, storms and the habits of pirates.

entries.name: Shopkeeper
entries.summary: Kept a general store or specialty shop in town, buying cheap and selling dear. Good with numbers and with difficult customers.

entries.name: Peddler
entries.summary: Sold small goods from a pack or cart from village to village. Knows the roads, local prices and a hundred sales tricks.

entries.name: Scholar
entries.summary: Studied history, lore or natural philosophy, perhaps tied to the Arcane University or a learned society. Better with books than with blades.

entries.name: Scribe
entries.summary: Copied books, wrote letters and kept records for a temple, a court or paying clients. Good handwriting and an eye for detail.

entries.name: Imperial clerk
entries.summary: Worked in the Empire's administration, filing records, taxes or petitions. The Nibenese bureaucracy runs on such patient, overlooked people.

entries.name: Alchemist
entries.summary: Brewed potions and poisons from herbs and creature parts. Knows ingredients, their effects and how dangerous a careless mix can be.

entries.name: Apothecary
entries.summary: Ran or worked in a shop selling remedies, ingredients and potions. Part merchant and part healer, trusted by the neighbourhood.

entries.name: Herbalist
entries.summary: Gathered wild plants and fungi to sell to alchemists and healers. Knows the countryside, its plants and its dangers well.

entries.name: Hedge healer
entries.summary: Treated wounds and illness with herbs and simple spells, often for poor folk who could not pay a temple. Practical, steady-handed and calm.

entries.name: Priest or priestess
entries.summary: Served at a chapel or temple, leading prayers, blessing the faithful and giving healing. Knows the gods' teachings and the troubles of a parish.

entries.name: Monastic novice
entries.summary: Lived in a priory or monastery under vows, working, praying and studying. Places like Weynon Priory near Chorrol shelter such quiet brothers.

entries.name: City guard
entries.summary: Kept the peace in a town or city, walking patrols, chasing thieves and guarding gates. Knows the law, the streets and the local troublemakers.

entries.name: Legion soldier
entries.summary: Served in the Imperial Legion, drilling, marching and fighting under Imperial orders. Knows discipline, formations and life in a fort.

entries.name: Mercenary
entries.summary: Sold a sword to whoever paid, from merchants to petty lords. Knows combat and contracts, and that loyalty lasts as long as the coin.

entries.name: Bodyguard
entries.summary: Guarded a wealthy merchant, noble or official from harm. Learned to read a crowd and to stand between a client and a knife.

entries.name: Fighters Guild member
entries.summary: Took contracts through the Fighters Guild: clearing pests, escorting travellers and guarding property. Proud of the guild, wary of rivals.

entries.name: Mages Guild apprentice
entries.summary: Studied magic at a Mages Guild hall, doing chores and lessons in hope of a recommendation to the Arcane University.

entries.name: Enchanter
entries.summary: Bound magic into weapons, armour and jewellery with soul gems. Skilled, well-paid and closely tied to the Mages Guild.

entries.name: Jeweller
entries.summary: Cut gems and worked gold and silver into rings, amulets and fine pieces. Knows stones, value and the people who can afford them.

entries.name: Arena combatant
entries.summary: Fought in the Imperial City Arena for crowds, wagers and fame. Knows showmanship, brutal combat and what it costs to keep winning.

entries.name: Courier
entries.summary: Carried letters and parcels between towns on foot or horseback. Knows the roads, shortcuts and how to keep going in bad weather.

entries.name: Minstrel
entries.summary: Earned coin singing, playing and telling stories in taverns and halls. Knows songs, legends and how to read an audience.

entries.name: Burglar
entries.summary: Broke into houses and shops by night, picking locks and taking what could be sold. Quiet, careful and good at disappearing.

entries.name: Pickpocket
entries.summary: Lifted purses in crowded markets and busy streets. Quick hands, a blank face and a talent for slipping away.

entries.name: Smuggler
entries.summary: Moved untaxed or illegal goods, such as moon sugar and skooma, past guards and customs. Knows hidden coves, bribes and boats.

entries.name: Fence
entries.summary: Bought stolen goods and sold them on quietly. Knows the worth of every item and keeps many secrets on both sides of the law.

entries.name: Beggar
entries.summary: Lived on alms in the streets, watching and listening. In Cyrodiil, beggars are often the eyes and ears of the Thieves Guild.

entries.name: Noble's retainer
entries.summary: Served a noble house as a guard, squire or steward. Knows court life, the household's secrets and how to stay in favour.

entries.name: Household servant
entries.summary: Worked as a maid, cook, valet or footman in a wealthy home. Knows the household's routines and secrets, and how to be unseen.

entries.name: Stablehand
entries.summary: Fed, groomed and cared for horses at a stable or inn. Knows mounts, tack and the travellers who come and go.

entries.name: Shepherd
entries.summary: Watched flocks of sheep or goats on hills and pastures, protecting them from wolves. Patient, outdoorsy and good with animals.

entries.name: Woodcutter
entries.summary: Felled trees and chopped firewood or timber for towns and builders. Strong, practical and used to working alone in the forest.
entries.eraNote: Not lore-friendly for a Bosmer raised under the Green Pact, which forbids harming Valenwood's plants.

entries.name: Vintner
entries.summary: Tended vines and made wine, perhaps at one of Skingrad's famous vineyards. Knows grapes, casks and buyers with good taste.

entries.name: Dockworker
entries.summary: Loaded and unloaded ships in a port like Anvil or the Imperial City Waterfront. Strong back, rough friends and knowledge of the docks.
